propDescriptions.xstyle: StyleX styles for root container

doc.description: Menu item component for compound mode. Re-exported from DropdownMenuItem for discoverability.
doc.name: ContextMenuItem

props.description: Icon to display before the label; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.
props.name: icon

props.description: Primary label text.
props.name: label

props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.
props.name: description

props.description: Callback when the item is selected. A keyboard activation arrives as a synthesized click carrying the key's modifiers. On a row with `href` it runs before the browser navigates and is skipped for a modified click (⌘, Ctrl, Shift, Alt, middle button), which is left to the browser.
props.name: onClick

props.description: Address the row navigates to. The row then renders as a real anchor with role="menuitem" (through LinkProvider), so a modified click or a middle click keeps the browser's meaning — a new tab — instead of running onClick.
props.name: href

props.description: Link target. Only used with href.
props.name: target

props.description: Link relationship. noopener noreferrer is added for target="_blank". Only used with href.
props.name: rel

props.description: Whether the row is unavailable. Disabled rows expose aria-disabled, remove link destinations, and suppress activation.
props.name: isDisabled

props.description: Additional content rendered after the label and description.
props.name: endContent

props.description: Whether activating the item closes the menu. Set false for an action that reports its result on the item itself.
props.name: hasCloseOnSelect

props.description: Visual variant. 'destructive' renders the label, description, and icon in the error color for dangerous actions (e.g. Delete).
props.name: variant

props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.
props.name: xstyle

props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitem". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.
props.name: ref

dense.description: Animates one element (x, y, scale, rotate, opacity) with Astryx's motion, without React.

paramDescriptions.element: The element to animate; one animator per element.

returnDescriptions.animate: (target, {velocity?}) => Promise<void>; springs on the state-change motion.
returnDescriptions.decay: ({x?, y?, scale?, rotate?, opacity?}) => Promise<void>; coasts from a release velocity.

bestPractices.description: Pass the release velocity to animate after a drag.
Read layout for the position mid-motion; use get.

usage.description: Spring with animate, fling with decay, follow a finger with set. Reduce Motion: a cross-fade on touch, at once with a mouse; decay keeps its momentum.

params.description: The element to animate. The animator writes its `translate`, `scale`, `rotate` and `opacity`, and while it moves an inline `will-change` for them, merged with any it already has and restored 500 ms after its last motion; nothing else, so lay it out and style it as usual. Use one animator per element: two on one element overwrite each other.
params.name: element

returns.description: Springs the given channels to `target` from wherever they are on screen, on the state-change motion Astryx's components use, and resolves when they arrive (or as soon as a later call takes them over). `x` and `y` are px, `scale` is 1 at the element's size, `rotate` is degrees and `opacity` runs from 0 to 1. Pass `velocity` (units per second, such as a drag's release velocity) to start with it; without it a channel keeps the velocity it has on screen, so interrupting a motion never jumps.
returns.name: animate
returns.type: (target: {x?, y?, scale?, rotate?, opacity?}, options?: {velocity?}) => Promise<void>

returns.description: Coasts the given channels from a release velocity in their units per second, slowing as a scroll view's momentum does, and resolves when they stop (or as soon as a later call takes any of them over); opacity stops at 0 or 1. The distance follows from the velocity: use it to fling something away, then remove or reset it.
returns.name: decay

returns.description: Puts the given channels at these values at once, ending their motion: follow a finger with it, frame by frame.
returns.name: set

returns.description: Every channel's value on screen now.
returns.name: get

returns.description: Every channel's velocity on screen now, in units per second.
returns.name: getVelocity

returns.description: Halts every channel where it is on screen.
returns.name: stop

returns.description: Stops every motion and lets the element go; the element keeps the values it shows. Call it when you remove the element or no longer animate it.
returns.name: destroy

accessibility.description: An animator moves an element; it adds no way to act. Give every action an animation stands for a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as a button that discards a card, and have it call `animate`, which Reduce Motion turns into a fade in place. Keep `decay` for a throw the person made: Reduce Motion keeps the momentum of a coast, as it continues that throw. Keep focus on an element that stays on screen: move it before you fling its element away.
accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology

accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, every call is planned for them. On a touch screen a move or a scale becomes a short opacity cross-fade: the element fades out where it was and fades back in where it lands. With a mouse it lands at once. A decay of `x` and `y` keeps its momentum, as it continues the throw the person made; a decay of `scale`, `rotate` or `opacity` is planned like a move. No option turns this off.
accessibility.name: Reduce Motion

bestPractices.description: Start every `animate` that follows a drag with the release velocity, so the element carries on as it was thrown.
Reach every state an animation shows without the animation too: a key, a button or a menu item that calls the same code.
`await` the promise before removing an element you animate out, and call `destroy` once it is gone.
Read the element’s position from layout while it moves: `get` gives the value on screen, wherever the motion runs.

usage.description: Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use, without React. `animate` springs an element to new values on the state-change motion, `decay` flings it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `set` moves it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. Use the `useAnimator` hook in React. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props.

dense.description: A drag that settles an element on snap points (px offsets) at the release, without React.

paramDescriptions.options.flickThreshold: px/s past which a release carries one snap point; 1008.
paramDescriptions.options.snapPoints: Ascending px offsets from the resting position.

returnDescriptions.settleTo: (index) settles without a drag: the keyboard path.

bestPractices.description: Wire settleTo to buttons and keys.
Rebuild a sheet or carousel with it.

usage.description: Nearest snap point, the next on a flick, the start when moving back; the settle keeps the release velocity. Sheets and carousels: use their props.

params.description: The element a drag moves. It moves along `axis` only, by translation, so lay it out at its resting position as usual.
params.name: element

params.description: The axis the element moves along.
params.name: options.axis

params.description: Offsets in px along `axis` from the element's resting position, such as `[0, 240, 480]`, sorted before use (`onSettle` and `settleTo` count in that order); an empty list makes the drag do nothing. Unlike BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, they are not fractions of the viewport.
params.name: options.snapPoints

params.description: A release faster than this, in px/s, carries to the next snap point in its direction. The default is the flick speed measured for UIKit's sheet.
params.name: options.flickThreshold

params.description: Called with the snap point's index once the element settles on it, after a drag or `settleTo`. A settle that a new drag interrupts calls nothing.
params.name: options.onSettle

returns.description: Settles the element on the snap point at `index` without a drag, then calls `onSettle`. Wire it to keys and buttons: it is the keyboard path. An index outside the snap points does nothing and warns in development.
returns.name: settleTo

returns.description: Removes every listener and stops the element where it is. Call it when you remove the element.
returns.name: destroy

accessibility.description: A drag is one way in, never the only one. Give each snap point a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as Expand and Collapse buttons, and call `settleTo` from it. When a position changes what the element shows, announce the change.
accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology

accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the settle after a touch drag becomes a short cross-fade into the snap point, as does any settle on a device whose primary pointer is coarse, such as a tablet; after a mouse or pen drag elsewhere it lands at once. `settleTo` fades on such a device and lands at once with a fine primary pointer. While the finger is down, the element still follows it.
accessibility.name: Reduce Motion

bestPractices.description: Offer the same positions without a drag: buttons or keys that call `settleTo`.
Keep the snap points few and far apart, so a release clearly picks one.
Use it for a sheet or a carousel: their own props already settle the way people expect.

usage.description: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Use the `useDragToSnapPoints` hook in React.

dense.description: Reports a drag on an element as values ({state, translation, velocity}), without React; a finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it, though a mouse or pen drag on selectable text selects it instead (give that text user-select: none). Returns {destroy}.

paramDescriptions.element: element to drag; the pan writes only its touch-action.
paramDescriptions.options.axis: 'x' | 'y': limit to one axis; the other is never reported and reads 0.
paramDescriptions.options.onPan: ({state, translation, velocity}): state 'began' | 'changed' | 'ended' | 'cancelled'; translation px since the drag began (no jump); velocity px/s, release velocity at 'ended', 0 at 'cancelled'.

returnDescriptions.destroy: () => void; removes every listener and the touch-action, cancels a drag in progress.

bestPractices.description: Move from translation + the offset at began, so the element moves with the finger from the claim.
Hand the ended velocity to the settling animation.
Call destroy when the element leaves the page.
Read layout on every changed event; use translation.

usage.description: Drag as values without React, for a surface you move. Claims at UIKit’s 10 pt. No keyboard path of its own (WCAG 2.5.7); Reduce Motion applies to what you animate. Prefer component props (BottomSheet snapPoints, Carousel hasSnap); in React, usePanGesture.

params.description: The element to drag. The pan writes the `touch-action` its axis needs on it and nothing else; it moves nothing itself.
params.name: element

params.description: Configuration object.
params.name: options

params.description: Limits the drag to one axis. A drag along the other axis is not reported, and that component of every value reads 0, so a scroll across it stays the page’s. Omit it to report both axes; a finger’s scroll that starts on the element then moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page.
params.name: options.axis

params.description: Called with `{state, translation, velocity}` as the drag begins, changes, ends at the release, or is cancelled. `state` is 'began', 'changed', 'ended' or 'cancelled'. `translation` is the movement since the drag began, in pixels, without the travel the drag needed to begin, so an element that follows it does not jump. `velocity` is in pixels per second; at 'ended' it is the release velocity, 0 when the finger rested before lifting, and at 'cancelled' it is 0.
params.name: options.onPan

returns.description: Removes every listener the pan added and its `touch-action`. A drag in progress is cancelled: `onPan` hears `cancelled`.
returns.name: destroy

accessibility.description: A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons, arrow keys or a menu.
accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology

accessibility.description: The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: a settle or a throw goes to its end without travel when the person asks for reduced motion.
accessibility.name: Reduce Motion

bestPractices.description: Move the element from `translation` added to where it was when the drag began, so it moves with the finger from the moment the drag claims it.
At `ended`, hand `velocity` to the animation that settles the element, so a flick carries on at the speed it was released.
Call `destroy` when the element leaves the page, so no listener outlives it.
Read the element’s layout on every `changed` event to place it; `translation` already says where the finger is.

usage.description: Reports a drag on an element as values, without React, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. Use the `usePanGesture` hook in React. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Its example is on the usePanGesture page: one draggable box, made once with the hook and once with createPanGesture.

dense.description: A collection's reorder behavior, for List's reorderable prop; ListItem itemKey on each row.

paramDescriptions.isReorderable: (key) => boolean; a rejected row has no handle, and at an end bounds the drop.
paramDescriptions.onReorder: ({key, to}) once per committed move; to is the index after the move.

returnDescriptions.reorderable: pass as List's reorderable prop; start(key) enters reorder mode from your own UI.

bestPractices.description: Stable data keys as itemKey; apply the move at once.
React's key or indexes as reorder keys.

usage.description: UIKit edit-mode reorder: hold then drag (finger; pen on a coarse primary pointer), drag at once (mouse; pen on a fine one); without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode (click, Space, Enter), arrows move, Escape ends.

params.description: Called once per committed move (a drop, or each move in reorder mode) with the moved item's key and its index after the move, in the full order of the collection's items. Apply it by rendering the items in their new order. A cancelled move calls nothing. The latest function given is the one called, so the object may be made on every render.
params.name: onReorder

params.description: Whether the item with this key can move. An item it rejects shows no handle and cannot be picked up; one at either end of the collection also bounds the others, so nothing drops beyond it and a keyboard move into it is refused. Every item moves without it.
params.name: isReorderable

returns.description: The collection's reorder behavior: pass it as `List`'s `reorderable` prop, with an `itemKey` on each `ListItem`. Make it once per collection (with useMemo); one made on every render still works. Its one method, `start(key)`, enters reorder mode for that item from your own UI (a Move item in its context menu, a toolbar button): the focus moves to its handle, as activating it does; a key that cannot move or is not mounted does nothing and warns in development. One object may serve several collections, each reordering on its own; `start` then uses the one mounted last.
returns.name: reorderable

bestPractices.description: Give each row a stable key from your data, a string or a number (`itemKey={item.id}`), and apply each move by rendering the items in their new order in the same task.
Use `isReorderable` for rows that must stay put, such as a pinned first row.
Offer reorder mode from your own UI too, such as a row's context menu, with `reorderable.start(item.id)`.
Use React's `key` as the reorder key, or index-based keys: a move changes every index after it.

usage.description: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.

dense.description: Makes a row's swipe actions: pass the value as swipe on Item or ListItem.

paramDescriptions.options.leading: Entries a drag toward the inline end uncovers, outermost last.
paramDescriptions.options.swipeBehavior: 'reveal' (rest open, entries tappable; default) or 'commit' (a full swipe fires the one entry of a side).
paramDescriptions.options.trailing: Entries a drag toward the inline start uncovers, outermost last.

bestPractices.description: Give each verb a second home in the row.
Several entries on a commit side.

usage.description: Touch accelerator for list rows; a mouse never swipes. Define once at module scope (handlers get {id, itemKey}) or in useMemo; no DOM work; its code ships only where it is imported.

params.description: The verbs a drag toward the inline end uncovers (rightward in left-to-right text), outermost last. Each is `{id, label, icon?, onActivate, isDisabled?, variant?: ItemSwipeActionVariant, hasRemoval?}`: `id` names the action, and the swipe's type carries the ids, so an id it does not have fails to compile. `label` names the state the verb reaches and is the button's accessible name. `onActivate({id, itemKey})` fires on a tap on a resting entry, on a full swipe, or on a `commit` release, once the row's content has left its box when the row slides out; `itemKey` is the `ListItem`'s, `undefined` on a plain `Item`. `hasRemoval` only says the row holds out after the action fires instead of springing back.
params.name: options.leading

params.description: The verbs a drag toward the inline start uncovers (leftward in left-to-right text), outermost last, in the same shape as `leading`.
params.name: options.trailing

params.description: What a swipe does, on both sides. `reveal` rests the row open with every entry a real button. As in a UIKit list, a fast release goes the way it moves, and a slow one past half the panel opens the row. A fling never fires an entry. A long drag fires the outermost: past the confirm point the row runs ahead and the outermost entry covers its place. Letting go there fires it. Backing out closes the row, and a disabled outermost entry never confirms. On a side with two or more entries, only a drag that starts on the open row fires. `commit` fires the one entry of a side on a full swipe, sliding the row out, with nothing resting and a presentational panel. On a side with two or more entries it fires none and warns in development.
params.name: options.swipeBehavior

returns.description: The row’s swipe actions, with nothing in them to read; its type carries the actions’ ids. Pass the value as `swipe` on `Item` or `ListItem`; a value made any other way swipes nothing. A new value with the same ids keeps an open row as it is, and one with other ids closes it.
returns.name: Swipe

accessibility.description: The swipe is a touch accelerator. A closed row’s panels are out of the accessibility tree and the tab order; an open row’s entries are real buttons under `reveal`, named by their labels, and Escape closes the row. Every verb must also be reachable through the row’s own content.
accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology

accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the row reaches its resting place with no travel or spring and cross-fades when a finger started the swipe.
accessibility.name: Reduce Motion

bestPractices.description: Give every swipe action a second home in the row, such as a menu or a button in endContent: a verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse.
Put the rows in a List, which clips them in the inline axis; any other container sets overflow-inline: clip once.
Give a `commit` side more than one entry: it fires none of them.

usage.description: Gives a list row the verbs a sideways swipe uncovers, the way a mail row reveals Archive and Delete on a phone: `const mail = createSwipe({trailing: [{id: 'archive', label: 'Archive', onActivate: ({itemKey}) => archive(itemKey)}]})`, then `<ListItem label="Inbox" itemKey={message.id} swipe={mail} />`. A finger, a pen or a trackpad’s two-finger swipe drags the row; a mouse never does. A plain function, not a hook, pure and cheap: define the swipe once at module scope, where each handler reads the row from `itemKey`, or in `useMemo` when its handlers need component state. A new value with the same ids neither closes an open row nor restarts its settle, and it does no DOM work. The swipe’s code comes with this function, so a row given `swipe` is swipeable at its first paint and an app that never imports it ships none of it.

dense.description: text input w/ calendar popover for picking a date

propDescriptions.calendar: calendar for typed + committed text, the popover, and the bottom sheet (months, leap months, era years; an era-change year follows the shown month, e.g. 平成31 in Jan 2019, 令和元 in Jul) (default: provider's, else 'gregory'); values stay Gregorian ISO; years are the calendar's, so set min/max on buddhist/roc fields; non-Gregorian-aligned calendars need Temporal (native or app-loaded polyfill), else Gregorian; non-gregory/iso8601 never shows the native control: popover fine / sheet coarse
propDescriptions.changeAction: async action after onChange; drives optimistic UI
propDescriptions.containerClassName: class name for the Field box; same target as containerXstyle
propDescriptions.containerStyle: inline styles for the Field box; same target as containerXstyle
propDescriptions.containerXstyle: Field box (label+control+status); also containerClassName/containerStyle. no effect in InputGroup or horizontal-labels FormLayout
propDescriptions.controlClassName: class name for the visual control box; same target as controlXstyle
propDescriptions.controlStyle: inline styles for the visual control box; same target as controlXstyle
propDescriptions.controlXstyle: visual control box (border/bg/icons), never the native input; also controlClassName/controlStyle. no root xstyle/className/style
propDescriptions.dateConstraints: custom constraint fns to disable specific dates
propDescriptions.disabledMessage: reason shown in a tooltip on hover/focus when disabled; describes the field's focusable controls
propDescriptions.entryErrorBehavior: 'complete'|'blur-or-enter': when the field's own rejection shows (not when validation runs; not React Aria validationBehavior; never changes status). complete: nonexistent/out-of-range date as soon as complete, unreadable/unfinished at Enter/blur. blur-or-enter: message, aria-invalid, styling, announcement and onEntryErrorChange report all wait for Enter/blur. Valid or emptied text clears at once; still-wrong edit keeps a shown error (blur-or-enter). Native refusals wait for Enter/blur under both. Default: nearest FormLayout defaultEntryErrorBehavior, else complete
propDescriptions.format: committed-value display: 'date_long' (default, March 21, 2026), 'date' (Mar 21, 2026), 'date_weekday' (Wed, Mar 21, 2026), 'system_date' (2026-03-21, always Gregorian ISO), or (iso)=>string; reuses Timestamp vocabulary; named formats write the field's calendar. Committed value only, not while typing.
propDescriptions.hasClear: Shows clear button when date is set. Clears value on click.
propDescriptions.isLabelHidden: visually hide label
propDescriptions.isLoading: loading state; stays focusable w/ aria-busy + spinner; blocks typing, picking, clearing
propDescriptions.label: label text
propDescriptions.labelTooltip: tooltip text via info icon at label end
propDescriptions.nativePicker: deprecated, use presentation: 'touch'='adaptive-native', 'always'='native', 'never'='adaptive-bottom-sheet'. still works as released, except that a calendar other than gregory or iso8601 never shows the native control; presentation wins if both set.
propDescriptions.numberOfMonths: months shown simultaneously in calendar popover
propDescriptions.onEntryErrorChange: (error|null) on each typed-rejection change: kind 'unreadable'|'incomplete'|'nonexistent'|'outOfRange' (min/max)|'unavailable' (dateConstraints), text, date (Gregorian ISO, outOfRange/unavailable); also on new min/max/dateConstraints/value, calendar pick, disable, Enter/blur; never twice for one rejection; null when the typed field leaves mid-rejection (presentation/pointer switch); with it an error status w/ message replaces the field's own message, re-announced once if unchanged when a rejection starts; never a rejection on native/touch pickers
propDescriptions.presentation: which surface draws the picker: 'adaptive-native' (default) = Astryx popover on fine, browser/OS on coarse w/ Astryx fallbacks; 'native' = browser/OS always, no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' = popover fine / Astryx sheet coarse; 'popover'/'bottom-sheet' force Astryx. every value opens a picker (no text-only value; that is TimeInput's). use non-native for weekStartsOn/numberOfMonths/dateConstraints. non-gregory/iso8601 calendar: native + adaptive-native become popover fine / sheet coarse; explicit 'native' warns in dev.
propDescriptions.status: error/warning/success status w/ message; a rejected date (typed or native) or kept unreadable/unfinished text shows its own error instead, unless onEntryErrorChange is set and status is an error w/ message
propDescriptions.statusVariant: How status message is placed: attached overlaps below input; detached floats below w/ spacing; tooltip hides the box and shows it on the status icon.
propDescriptions.weekStartsOn: first day of week in calendar (0=Sunday, or name e.g. "mon")

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels + descriptions so users understand what date is expected.
Use min, max, and dateConstraints to restrict selectable dates to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the date is optional so the user can reset it.
Show a loading state with changeAction when the date triggers a server-side save.

On a fine pointer the field follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a dialog popup, as in the APG date picker combobox: ArrowDown or Alt+ArrowDown opens the calendar, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the field.
Use inside InputGroup for a short static prefix or suffix, such as a due-date hint.
Use a DateInput for free-form text that does not represent a calendar date.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Rely on the calendar alone; the text input lets users type dates directly, which is faster for known dates.
Wrap a disabled DateInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

usage.description: DateInput lets the user type or pick a date from a calendar popover. Use for scheduling, deadlines, booking dates, or any form field needing a calendar date.

props.description: Label text.
props.name: label

props.description: Visually hide the label.
props.name: isLabelHidden

props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.
props.name: description

props.description: Show an "(optional)" indicator next to the label.
props.name: isOptional

props.description: Mark the field as required.
props.name: isRequired

props.description: Disable the input and calendar. The field stays focusable and exposes `aria-disabled`; typing and opening are blocked.
props.name: isDisabled

props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled DateInput in Tooltip.
props.name: disabledMessage

props.description: Selected date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
props.name: value

props.description: Callback invoked when the selected date changes.
props.name: onChange

props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Drives optimistic UI updates via useTransition.
props.name: changeAction

props.description: Whether the input is in a loading state. The field stays focusable and exposes `aria-busy` with a spinner; typing, picking, and clearing are blocked until loading ends.
props.name: isLoading

props.description: Minimum selectable date (YYYY-MM-DD).
props.name: min

props.description: Maximum selectable date (YYYY-MM-DD).
props.name: max

props.description: Array of custom constraint functions that disable specific dates.
props.name: dateConstraints

props.description: Placeholder text shown in the text input. A caller placeholder replaces the calendar format hint.
props.name: placeholder

props.description: Size of the input control.
props.name: size

props.description: Status indicator object for error, warning, or success states with a message. For a date the field rejects, typed or picked in the native control, and for unreadable or unfinished text that Enter or blur keeps, the field shows its own error message instead; with onEntryErrorChange, an error status with a message shows in place of that message. A warning or success never replaces a rejection.
props.name: status

props.description: Called each time the field's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. kind is 'unreadable', 'incomplete' (part of a date that Enter or blur cannot finish), 'nonexistent' (a date the calendar does not have), 'outOfRange' (before min or after max), or 'unavailable' (a day dateConstraints rules out); text is the typed text; date is the Gregorian ISO date the text names, for 'outOfRange' and 'unavailable'. It also runs when a new min, max, dateConstraints, or value, a calendar pick, disabling the field, or Enter or blur changes the rejection, and never twice for the same rejection; it reports null when the typed field leaves while its rejection stands, as when a presentation or pointer change shows the native or touch picker. With it, an error status with a message replaces the field's own message, and a rejection that starts under an unchanged error message announces that message once. The native and touch pickers take no typed text, so it never reports a rejection there.
props.name: onEntryErrorChange
props.type: (error: {kind: 'unreadable' | 'incomplete' | 'nonexistent' | 'outOfRange' | 'unavailable', text: string, date?: ISODateString} | null) => void

props.description: When the field shows its own entry error: a typed date it rejects, as onEntryErrorChange reports it. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. 'complete' shows a date the calendar does not have, or one outside min, max, or dateConstraints, as soon as the typed date is complete, and unreadable or unfinished text at Enter or blur. 'blur-or-enter' holds every rejection until Enter or blur: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report then appear together. Under both values, an edit that makes the text a date or empties it clears the error at once; under 'blur-or-enter', an edit that leaves the text wrong keeps the shown error until the next Enter or blur. A date the native control refuses shows at Enter or blur under both values. The field's own value wins over the nearest FormLayout's defaultEntryErrorBehavior.
props.name: entryErrorBehavior

props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: numberOfMonths

props.description: First day of week in Astryx calendar surfaces. A number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday) or a three-letter day name; native pickers remain browser/OS-owned.
props.name: weekStartsOn

props.description: How the committed date value is displayed. Named values are reused from Timestamp's format vocabulary: 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2026', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2026', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2026', 'system_date' shows '2026-03-21'. 'date', 'date_long', and 'date_weekday' write the date in the field's calendar; 'system_date' stays the Gregorian ISO date. A function receives the ISO value and returns a custom string; the field cannot re-commit text it cannot read back. Applies only to the committed value, never to text being typed.
props.name: format

props.description: The calendar the text field reads and writes dates in, and the calendar its popover and bottom sheet show. value, onChange, min, and max stay Gregorian ISO dates. People type a date the way the locale writes it in this calendar, in any decimal digits; the field reports a date only once it is complete, and names a date the calendar does not have. Years are years of this calendar: a Buddhist field reads 2026 as Buddhist year 2026, so set min and max on Buddhist and Minguo calendar fields to catch a Gregorian year typed by mistake. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal, native or a polyfill the application loads; without it the field shows Gregorian dates. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, a presentation that would show the native date control shows the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, because the native control is Gregorian; the bottom sheet shows the months, leap months, and era years of the calendar. A year in which the era changes is labeled with the era of the shown month, such as 平成31 in January 2019 and 令和元 in July.
props.name: calendar

props.description: Which surface draws the date picker. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's calendar popover on a fine pointer and the browser/OS picker (input type=date) on a coarse pointer, keeping Astryx fallbacks where a native control cannot express the value; 'native' always uses the browser/OS picker with no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses the popover on a fine pointer and Astryx's bottom-sheet picker on a coarse pointer; 'popover' and 'bottom-sheet' force that Astryx surface on every pointer. Every value opens a picker; a typed-only field is TimeInput's alone. Use a non-native presentation for a field that needs weekStartsOn, numberOfMonths or dateConstraints, none of which a native picker can express. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'native' and 'adaptive-native' use the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, and an explicit 'native' warns in development.
props.name: presentation

props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'adaptive-bottom-sheet'). With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'touch' and 'always' use the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer.

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what date is expected.
Use min, max, and dateConstraints to restrict selectable dates to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the date is optional so the user can reset it.
Show a loading state with changeAction when the date triggers a server-side save.

On a fine pointer the field follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a dialog popup, as in the APG date picker combobox: ArrowDown or Alt+ArrowDown opens the calendar, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the field.
Use DateInput inside InputGroup when adding a short static prefix or suffix, such as a due-date hint.
Use a DateInput for free-form text that does not represent a calendar date.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Rely on the calendar alone; the text input lets users type dates directly, which is faster for known dates.
Wrap a disabled DateInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, a presentation that would show native controls shows the popovers on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, because the native date control is Gregorian; the Date panel of the bottom sheet shows the months, leap months, and era years of the calendar. A year in which the era changes is labeled with the era of the shown month, such as 平成31 in January 2019 and 令和元 in July.

props.description: Status indicator object for error, warning, or success states with a message. For a date the field rejects, typed or picked in the native control, and for unreadable or unfinished text that Enter or blur keeps, the field shows its own error message instead; with onEntryErrorChange, an error status with a message shows in place of that message. A warning or success never replaces a rejection. A typed time the time segment rejects shows once it is complete, or at Enter or blur, and stays in the field; its own error message shows unless the date segment shows its message or an error status with a message shows in its place.

props.description: Called each time the date segment's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. kind is 'unreadable', 'incomplete' (part of a date that Enter or blur cannot finish), 'nonexistent' (a date the calendar does not have), 'outOfRange' (before the date of min or after the date of max), or 'unavailable' (a day dateConstraints rules out); text is the typed text; date is the Gregorian ISO date the text names, for 'outOfRange' and 'unavailable'. It also runs when a new min, max, dateConstraints, or value, a calendar pick, disabling the field, or Enter or blur changes the rejection, and never twice for the same rejection; it reports null when the typed field leaves while its rejection stands, as when a presentation or pointer change shows the native or touch picker. With it, an error status with a message replaces the field's own message, and a rejection that starts under an unchanged error message announces that message once. The native and touch pickers take no typed text, so it never reports a rejection there.

'blur-or-enter' holds every rejection until Enter or blur in its segment: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the date segment's onEntryErrorChange report then appear together. Under both values, an edit the field accepts or that empties the segment clears the error at once; under 'blur-or-enter', an edit that leaves the entry wrong keeps the shown error until the next Enter or blur. bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateTimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what datetime is expected.
Use min and max to restrict selectable datetimes to valid ranges.

Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.

Use DateTimeInput when only a time is needed; use TimeInput instead.

usage.description: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection in one field. With reduced motion the dialog never slides or scales in: on a touch screen it fades in, in 200 ms or less, and with a mouse it appears at once. Choose: Dialog for centered decisions/short forms, Drawer for full-height side detail, BottomSheet for block-axis sheets, docked layout column to reflow instead of float. usage.description:
A side panel that floats above page content for inspectors and detail views: the "click a table row, see its details" pattern. Unlike a docked panel it overlays the layout instead of reflowing it. Works on desktop and touch: the width budget applies on desktop and the panel preserves a 56px page reveal below 640px without exceeding the width budget. Escape closes the drawer (unless purpose is required) and focus returns to the element that opened it. Entry/exit slide animation respects prefers-reduced-motion. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), a tap or a drag that lands while the drawer is still sliding in reaches nothing (for a drawer without a scrim, only one on the panel: the page stays live), and the drawer finishes sliding in; keys and assistive technology stay live, and a mouse or a trackpad still clicks: at once when it was the last pointer used, otherwise once it moves. Stacking contract: sibling drawers stack last-opened on top, Escape closes only the topmost, and closing peels innermost-first; render them as siblings, never nested.

Like Dialog, the drawer is a container: its content area is inset by --spacing-4 (16px) by default, by the padding prop, or by a theme's padding on drawer. Compose the header, body, and footer the way Dialog does, with a Layout: DrawerHeader in the header slot (it shows a close button when you pass it onOpenChange, like DialogHeader), the body in LayoutContent, and actions in LayoutFooter. The Layout redistributes the inset to those regions so they line up on one content line, and the header is not inset twice. A lone Section child also escapes the inset. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so give every drawer a visible way to close, especially a non-modal one, which has no scrim to click. Put data-autofocus on the control that should receive focus on open.

Choosing a surface: use Dialog for a centered decision or short form, Drawer for full-height side detail that keeps the page in sight, BottomSheet for block-axis sheets on touch, and a docked panel (a layout column) when content should reflow the page instead of floating over it.

Theming: the panel is the single stable target (astryx-drawer, with data-side reflecting side), and the scrim is the panel's native ::backdrop. DrawerHeader exposes astryx-drawer-header targets for its row, slots, and close icon.

bestPractices.description: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented so users can scan options quickly.
Focus returns on close, to the trigger or a stand-in (a sheet uses its own return); no off switch. Focus elsewhere in onOpenChange to redirect it.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
For a short, flat action set, use presentation="bottom-sheet" when product policy calls for a modal touch surface.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the same short action set should remain anchored on pointer layouts and become a BottomSheet on compact coarse-pointer layouts.
For a hierarchy that cannot fit as adjacent flyouts on a compact touch surface, a product may explicitly use a drill-in interaction with a Back action.
Choose presentation explicitly in product code. A compact, coarse-pointer, hover-free media query is one useful policy, but DropdownMenu does not impose a universal device breakpoint.
When the content is no longer a short list of immediate actions, reevaluate the interaction and choose a component that matches the actual task; content traits alone do not determine the component.
Use a DropdownMenu for navigation; use a navigation component instead.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

props.description: Render the control the menu hangs off — an IconButton, a chip, an avatar, a list row — instead of the built-in Button. Spread the given props onto it: they carry the press model (a mouse opens on press-down, a finger or a pen opens as it presses), the keyboard opens, the toggle click, and `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`id`; the menu is then named by that control through `aria-labelledby`. Compound children currently support popover only. Omitted, the menu is anchored, and under a finger or a pen, on every device, its trigger opens as it is pressed (inside a scroll view, after the 150 ms content-touch delay), and the opening finger picks after moving 10 px. doc.description: A single menu row that reveals a nested flyout of its own items. The row adopts DropdownMenuItem semantics (label / icon / description / isDisabled); its children become the flyout content. Opens inline-end with viewport auto-flip; Right/Enter/Space opens and focuses the first item, Left/Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger (Right/Left swap in RTL). On a phone (a coarse pointer, decided when the menu opened) the row drills in instead: its rows replace the menu's rows in the same box, led by a Back row named "Back to <parent>", and Back, Escape or ArrowLeft return to the row. Host attributes and DOM event handlers (aria-*, data-*, id) reach the trigger row, the element carrying role="menuitem" and aria-haspopup="menu"; a caller's handlers run after the row's own, except for the keys that open the flyout (the open arrow, Enter, Space) and a click on a disabled row. For data-driven menus, give a menu item a nested `items` array instead of using this component directly.
doc.name: DropdownMenuSubMenu

bestPractices.description: Use attached status below bordered inputs when the message belongs to that input.
Use detached status for controls like checkboxes, switches, and custom controls where overlap would be visually awkward.
Use FieldStatus for general alerts or page-level notices; use Banner or Toast instead.

A field's status is announced when it first appears and when its message or type changes, not again when a repeated submit fails with the same errors. On such a repeated submit, with the errors unchanged, announce it once from the form with useAnnounce, for example announce(`${errors.length} errors. ${errors[0]}`, 'assertive'), and move focus to the first invalid field. On a first failed submit the fields announce their own errors, so the form adds no announcement.

props.description: The state the form treats as its default, so only the exception shows an optional/required indicator. With "optional", only fields marked isRequired show an indicator; with "required", only fields marked isOptional do. A field that restates the default shows nothing. Under "required" the unmarked fields also expose aria-required so screen readers match the visual default; aria-required only, never the native required attribute. CheckboxInput, Switch and CheckboxList are the exception: an unchecked box, an off switch or an empty group is an answer, so they take no required state from the default. props.description: When DateInput, DateTimeInput, TimeInput, and NumberInput fields in the layout show their own entry errors: a date, time, or number the field rejects. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. 'complete' shows each error at the field's own moment. 'blur-or-enter' holds the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report until Enter or blur; an edit that makes the entry valid or empty still clears the error at once. NumberInput shows its errors only at Enter or blur under both values. A field's own entryErrorBehavior wins. A nested FormLayout replaces the default for its fields, and unset there means 'complete'. Content in a layer, such as a Dialog opened from the form, starts without it. Leave unset for 'complete'.

Pair minWidth with max to cap the count on wide screens. In a container narrower than minWidth, one column shrinks to the container width, with or without max.
{minWidth} alone keeps column width; fewer items than tracks leave empty tracks (2 items, 880px, minWidth 280 -> empty 3rd column). To let items grow: repeat: 'fit', or max <= item count.

Use `columns={4}` for a row that must work on small screens; a number never reflows and renders four narrow tracks on a phone. Reserve numbers for rows that must stay fixed, such as a 7-day week.

Provide a dashed underline on text triggers so users know the element is hoverable.
Use the hook API (useHoverCard) when you need more control over timing or placement.
Leave touchTrigger on auto so a tap opens the card on triggers that do nothing else, and stays out of the way on triggers that perform an action.
Place critical actions or required information inside a hover card; users may miss content that only appears on hover.
Use a hover card when a simple Tooltip or Popover would suffice.
Use a HoverCard for content the user must interact with; it disappears when the cursor leaves.
Put the trigger inside SVG <foreignObject>: Chromium cannot anchor to it, so the card opens at the viewport corner. Use an HTML trigger positioned over the SVG node.

Prefer a block context over a direct

, heading, or link placement. Those placements work when necessary through a corrective portal, but DOM/tab order may differ.

bestPractices.description: Use built-in meanings when available; they adapt to theme changes automatically.

Override icons via theme, not globally: defineTheme({icons: {close: <XMarkIcon />}}) scopes the swap to the active <Theme>; extends shallow-merges into derived themes. registerIcons() mutates a global registry and warns in dev: app bootstrap only, not a library theming seam.

Size-aware artwork: a theme/registered entry may be a pure sync function of {size, variant}, e.g. info: ({size}) => <InfoIcon weight={size === 'sm' ? 'bold' : 'regular'} />. Icon passes its rendered size; getIcon/useIcon/getIconRegistry/theme.icons read it at md. A null result draws nothing (no fallback). No hooks, DOM measurement, or browser/mutable state.
Pair icons with text labels for accessibility; icon-only elements need an accessible label.
For a meaningful standalone icon (no adjacent text), set an accessible name via `label`: sets role="img" + aria-label, unhides icon.
Use color tokens for icon colors, not hardcoded hex values.
Be mindful of context; decorative icons in compact components can distract rather than help.
Use icons as the sole means of conveying meaning; always provide a text alternative.
Resize icons with arbitrary pixel values; use the provided size props.
Mix icon styles (e.g. outline and filled) within the same context.
Render raw SVG elements; always wrap in Icon for consistent sizing and color.
`name` prop, which does not exist. Use `icon` to specify which icon to render.

usage.description: Icons are small visual symbols that represent actions, objects, or concepts. They improve scannability and reinforce meaning alongside text. Supports both direct SVG components and built-in meanings that adapt to the active theme.

props.description: Built-in meaning, or any SVG component from your icon library (`icon={TrashIcon}`). Built-in meanings: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, upload, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. A namespaced key such as `richtext:bold` names a glyph that one component or library registers, and a theme can replace it by key; a namespaced key that nothing registers renders nothing. For any icon not in this list, pass an SVG component directly (e.g. import from lucide-react or @heroicons/react). Note: this prop is called `icon`, not `name`; a call with only `name` renders that glyph and warns in development.
props.name: icon

props.description: Color variant mapped to Astryx icon color tokens. Semantic values (primary through warning) follow the role, and inherit uses the surrounding text color. On the web, Icon also accepts the palette values blue, red, green, gray, cyan, teal, yellow, orange, pink, and purple, which pick a non-semantic hue.
props.name: color

props.description: Icon size. xsm, sm, md, and lg are 12, 16, 20, and 24px at a 16px root and scale with the root font size; a theme sets a size's glyph dimension with width and height, in px or rem, on components.icon['size:sm'] (and the other sizes). An explicit value wins. When omitted, Icon uses the nearest default supplied by an owning Astryx component for its icon slot, then falls back to md when no contextual default exists.
props.name: size

props.description: Requests the active theme's alternate artwork for a built-in meaning, such as 'filled'. Names come from IconVariantMap, which an application augments from @astryxdesign/core/Icon; Astryx defines none. The theme's icon entry receives the variant only when the active theme lists it in iconVariants (and, for an entry the theme inherited, the theme that defined the entry lists it too); otherwise it draws its normal artwork. Ignored by an icon component passed directly. Selects artwork only: it is not written to the DOM and has no theming selector.

bestPractices.description: Use built-in meanings when available; they adapt to theme changes automatically.

Override icons through the theme, not globally: defineTheme({icons: {close: <XMarkIcon />}}) scopes the swap to the active <Theme>, and extends shallow-merges it into derived themes. registerIcons() mutates a process-wide registry and warns in dev, so keep it for app bootstrap rather than making it a library's theming seam.

To match artwork to the rendered size, make a theme or registered icon entry a pure, synchronous function of {size, variant}: defineTheme({icons: {info: ({size}) => <InfoIcon weight={size === 'sm' ? 'bold' : 'regular'} />}}). Icon passes the size it renders at; getIcon(), useIcon(), getIconRegistry() and theme.icons read the function at size md. A function that returns null draws nothing instead of falling back to the default icon. Do not use hooks, measure the DOM, or read browser or mutable state inside it.
Pair icons with text labels for accessibility; icon-only elements need an accessible label.
For a meaningful standalone icon (no adjacent text), give it an accessible name via the `label` prop: it sets role="img" + aria-label and unhides the icon.
Use color tokens for icon colors, not hardcoded hex values.
Be mindful of context; decorative icons in compact components can distract rather than help.
Use icons as the sole means of conveying meaning; always provide a text alternative.
Resize icons with arbitrary pixel values; use the provided size props.
Mix icon styles (e.g. outline and filled) within the same context.
Render raw SVG elements; always wrap in Icon for consistent sizing and color.
Pass a `name` prop; Icon uses `icon` (not `name`) to specify which icon to render.

dense.description: Decorative selection visuals: the mark on a chosen option, the checkbox box, the radio circle. Rendered by Selector/CheckboxInput/RadioList/menu rows. Replace one by name via defineTheme({indicators}) and every component drawing it follows.

bestPractices.description: Prefer the canonical `components['checkbox-indicator']` override first. Replacing the component is the heavier path, for when the shape itself is wrong.

Match the shipped replacement-content branch with `isRenderable(children)`, not `children != null` or `children ?? mark`. The helper is shallow: it excludes nullish values, booleans, and the empty string, while React elements and containers take the replacement path even when their descendants render nothing. The owner passes `children={isBusy && <Spinner/>}`, so a nullish check deletes the state mark whenever the value is `false` (#4893).
A replacement must set aria-hidden. The owner supplies role and accessible name; a visible indicator would be announced twice.
Use theme tokens for every color, radius, and border width in a replacement. Run `astryx docs tokens` for the set.

Render a single root ELEMENT with the border-radius the focus ring should follow. The owner paints the standard ring onto the indicator at focus time (useIndicatorFocusRing) and outline picks up its radius; the ring is never missing (WCAG 2.4.7), only mis-shaped if the root lacks a radius. Do not draw a focus ring yourself.
Thread hover or pressed state in as props. Interaction state reaches an indicator through the owner's CSS ancestor marker.

Assume you are only mounted when selected. The host renders the indicator unconditionally and passes `state` in every state; that is what lets a replacement draw where the default draws nothing (a radio's empty circle on an unchosen row).

bestPractices.description: Reach for the canonical `components['checkbox-indicator']` override first. Replacing the component is the heavier path, for when the shape itself is wrong.

Match the shipped replacement-content branch with `isRenderable(children)`, not `children != null` or `children ?? mark`. The helper is deliberately shallow: it excludes nullish values, booleans, and the empty string, while React elements and containers take the replacement path even when their descendants render nothing. The owning control passes `children={isBusy && <Spinner/>}`, so a nullish check deletes the state mark whenever that value is `false` (#4893).
A replacement must set aria-hidden. The owning control provides the role and accessible name; a visible indicator would be announced twice.
Use theme tokens for every color, radius, and border width in a replacement. Run `astryx docs tokens` for the set.

Render a single root ELEMENT, and let it keep the border-radius you want the focus ring to follow. A control whose real input is visually hidden cannot show focus on that input, so the owner paints the standard ring onto the indicator element itself at focus time (useIndicatorFocusRing), and `outline` then picks up that element's radius. A replacement needs no cooperation and can forget nothing: the ring is never missing (WCAG 2.4.7), it is only the wrong shape if the root has no radius of its own. Do not draw a focus ring yourself; the owner already did.
Thread hover or pressed state in as props. Interaction state reaches an indicator through the owner's CSS ancestor marker, so hovering the row tints the control with no props involved.

Assume you are only mounted when selected. The host renders its indicator unconditionally and passes `state`, in every state; that is what lets a replacement draw where the default draws nothing (a radio's empty circle on an unchosen row). Drawing nothing in a state is a decision the indicator makes, not one the host makes for it.

While the row is selected it writes aria-current on the control unless the control has its own; do not set the row's value on the control yourself.

props.description: Swipe actions for touch, made by createSwipe({leading?, trailing?, swipeBehavior?}): the verbs a sideways drag uncovers on each side, outermost last, each `{id, label, icon?, onActivate({id, itemKey}), isDisabled?, variant?: ItemSwipeActionVariant, hasRemoval?}`; `itemKey` is the `ListItem`'s, `undefined` on a plain `Item`. `leading` is uncovered by a drag toward the inline end, `trailing` toward the inline start. A finger, a pen or a trackpad's two-finger swipe drags the row; a mouse drag and a mouse wheel's notches never do, and a mostly vertical drag stays the scroller's. An open row closes on a touch tap on its own content, which activates nothing and paints no press, on a press elsewhere, when the list or page scrolls with focus outside it, and on Escape. The gesture is a touch accelerator and never a row's only path to a verb: a verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse, so every entry must also be reachable through the row's own content. Served on a row whose role permits interactive descendants (a listitem, a row with no role) and not on an option, a menu item, or a row that is the enlarged target of a native radio. The element containing the rows clips in the inline axis with overflow-inline: clip — List does; any other host does it once. `hasRemoval` only says the row holds out after the action fires instead of springing back. The swipe is the same on every device: a finger or a pen swipes the row whatever the primary pointer, a touchscreen laptop's included, and so does a trackpad's two-finger swipe, which moves the row with the fingers and lets it go at their speed; a mouse never does. The swipe's code comes with createSwipe, so a row given swipe is swipeable at its first paint and an app that never imports createSwipe ships none of it. Define the swipe once at module scope, or in useMemo when its handlers need component state. A new value with the same ids neither closes an open row nor restarts its settle; one with other ids closes it.

usage.description: Layer utilities provide the app-level provider used by overlay systems. Use LayerProvider at the app root for toast/layer configuration; use higher-level Popover, HoverCard, or Tooltip APIs for most overlay UI. Rendered layer content, not the provider’s application subtree, uses theme body text defaults and exits ancestor surface/group membership. Establish intentional groups and complete required providers inside each layer. Every anchored layer keeps a gutter from each viewport edge — the spacing-4 step or the device safe-area inset, whichever is larger — and is capped to the viewport, never to the room beside its trigger: an explicit width renders at its size, flips when it does not fit beside the trigger, and slides into view when it fits on neither side. An app that floats a persistent bar over a viewport edge declares it once as inset on LayerProvider (blockStart, blockEnd, inlineStart, inlineEnd); each edge adds to that edge’s gutter for every anchored layer and moves the toast viewport by the same amount, and defaults to zero. The inset is app configuration, not a theme value.

bestPractices.description: Write descriptive, concise link text that clearly communicates the destination.
Set `isStandalone` when the link appears outside of inline text, so it receives proper base font sizing.
Put a Link inside a <Text maxLines> to truncate it with the surrounding text; inside a clamped Text the link flows in the text's lines.

Only set `label` when the link content is not descriptive text (e.g. an icon-only link). For text links, the visible text is already the accessible name; adding `label` overrides it for screen readers, which is harmful.
Use Link for actions that do not navigate; use a Button instead.

Set `label` on text links; `aria-label` prevents assistive technology from reading the actual link content.
Give a Link inside a clamped Text its own `display` or `maxLines`, or render it as a button (`onClick` with no `href`), and expect the outer clamp to cut it; that Link keeps its own box.
Put a Link with block-level content, such as an HStack with an icon, inside a clamped Text; block content breaks the clamp. Clamp a text-only Link, or place the composed Link outside the clamp.

props.description: The handle from useAnimatedLayout({containerRef}). With it, when rows are inserted, removed or reordered, an inserted row enters, a removed row collapses in place, a row that crosses rows moving the other way rides above them with the surface color behind it, and the rows after a change and the content after the list, up to that container, glide to their new places, all on one shared motion, under every pointer. Under Reduce Motion nothing travels. A row is identified by its itemKey: a row without one changes at once. Without a handle the list changes at once.
props.name: animatedLayout

props.description: Makes the rows reorderable, with the object createReorderable({onReorder, isReorderable}) makes: each ListItem with an itemKey gets a reorder handle at its end, and each committed move calls onReorder once with the row's key and its index after the move ({key, to}); render the rows in the new order to apply it. A row the object's isReorderable rejects has no handle and keeps its place; one at either end of the list also bounds the others. The object may be made on every render. On a touch screen, a finger held still on a handle for a moment picks up its row (a flick on it still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near the edges, and on release the rows rearrange, gliding to their new places. A mouse drags a handle at once with the same copy and line, and the rows take their places without motion; a drag reports once, at the drop, and a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. In reorder mode the line marks the row's new place after each move. Without a drag, the handle is a toggle: a click, Space or Enter turns on reorder mode for its row (aria-pressed), in which each Up or Down arrow moves the row a place at once and reports it, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves. Each move is announced once it renders, with the row's place and its neighbours ('Milk, position 3 of 5, after Eggs, before Bread'), and a move into a row that keeps its place is refused and announced. While the mode is on, a hint anchored to the handle shows the moves and Done as buttons that do what the keys do, so a row can also be reordered by taps alone. The object's start(key) enters the same mode from your own UI, such as a row's context menu. A disabled row's handle stays focusable but moves nothing.
props.name: reorderable

props.description: Where each row's text, dividers, and hover and selection backgrounds sit, relative to the list's edges and the container around it. 'padded' keeps text inside each row's padding, so it starts a little in from a heading above the list and backgrounds have room around it. 'flush' drops the rows' side padding: text starts on the heading's line, and dividers and backgrounds stop at the row's content, with no room beyond it on either side. It works anywhere and suits static rows. 'outset' puts text on the heading's line and reaches dividers and backgrounds a little past it into the container's padding; it suits interactive rows in a container. 'bleed' puts text on the heading's line and reaches dividers and backgrounds to the container's edges, like Table rows in a Card. Rows are square, except that when the list is the first or last child of a rounded Card or Dialog that holds no other Table or bleeding List deeper inside, its first row (when it has no header) or last row takes the container's corner, less the container padding above or below it. A row's first content is what lines up with the heading: its marker, icon, or avatar when it has one, otherwise its label. 'outset' and 'bleed' reach into the padding of the nearest container that shares its padding: a Card, Section, Dialog, or BottomSheet, or a transparent container such as a Layout region with explicit padding or a padded ScrollableArea. Place the List directly in that container's padding: padding that Stack, Center, or your own styles add in between is not counted. Drawers and the automatic padding of LayoutContent and LayoutPanel aren't supported yet. With no such container, including in a Popover, they look like 'padded'. In a container with less padding than the rows' own, text starts a little after the heading's line. A theme's inline padding on `item` replaces the row padding of every value, including the zero padding of flush.

props.name: description

props.description: Content rendered before the label area (e.g. icon, avatar).
props.name: startContent

props.description: Content rendered after the label area (e.g. badge, chevron).
props.name: endContent

props.description: Click handler; enables the invisible button pattern.
props.name: onClick

props.description: Ref to a nested control (e.g. a checkbox in startContent) that owns the item's keyboard access and action. The row becomes an enlarged click/tap target that delegates surface clicks to it (useClickableContainer) and renders no invisible button/anchor, so the row adds no second tab stop (WCAG 4.1.2). Mutually exclusive with onClick/href; those are ignored when set. While the row is selected it writes aria-current on the control unless the control has its own; do not set the row's value on the control yourself.
props.name: interactiveRef

props.description: Link URL; enables the invisible anchor pattern. The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.
props.name: href

props.description: Link target attribute, only applicable when href is provided. target="_blank" automatically adds noopener noreferrer.
props.name: target

props.description: Link relationship tokens. noopener noreferrer are merged automatically for target="_blank".
props.name: rel

props.description: Vertical alignment of the start and end content against the label, passed through to Item unchanged. `first-line` keeps a small mark (a status dot, an icon) level with the first line of a wrapped label. See Item.align.
props.name: align

props.description: Disabled state; interactive rows stay keyboard-reachable, expose aria-disabled, and cannot activate.
props.name: isDisabled

props.description: Selected state; marks the item as the current one with aria-current="true" (a list item cannot carry aria-selected). On a row with onClick or href, the marker sits on the row's button or link, which takes focus; on a row with interactiveRef, on the control it delegates to.
props.name: isSelected

props.description: The row's item key, a string or a number from the data (the shape Table's idKey returns). It is the row's identity for the list's animated layout (List animatedLayout): with a handle, the list matches rows by it to animate inserts, removals and moves, and a row without one changes at once. In a reorderable List (List reorderable), it is the key the reorderable object's onReorder reports and isReorderable is asked about, and a row without one has no reorder handle and keeps its place. Separate from React's key.
props.name: itemKey

props.description: Swipe actions for touch, made by createSwipe({leading?, trailing?, swipeBehavior?}) and passed to Item with this row's itemKey added: the verbs a sideways drag uncovers on each side, each `{id, label, icon?, onActivate({id, itemKey}), isDisabled?, variant?: ItemSwipeActionVariant, hasRemoval?}`, where `itemKey` is this row's. One definition at module scope serves every row. See Item.swipe; List clips its rows in the inline axis for them. A verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse, so give each entry a second home in the row.
props.name: swipe

props.description: Deprecated (DEP-0017): pass swipe={createSwipe({leading, trailing})} instead. Each entry is `{id?, label, icon?, onActivate, isDisabled?, variant?: 'neutral' | 'accent' | 'destructive', hasRemoval?}`. Passed through to Item unchanged; astryx upgrade rewrites static uses.
props.name: swipeActions

props.description: Deprecated (DEP-0017): pass swipeBehavior in createSwipe's options instead. Passed through to Item unchanged; astryx upgrade rewrites static uses.
props.name: swipeBehavior

dense.description: Renders markdown string as Astryx-styled components. Use for user-generated content, AI responses, docs. Headings, lists, tables, code, citations w/ consistent styling.

propDescriptions.autolink: 'gfm'. Opt-in GFM autolinking: bare URLs (https?://, www.), <scheme:url>, <email>, user@host. Skips code, code blocks, existing links. Default: off.
propDescriptions.citationStyle: 'label'|'number'. label=chip w/ title+icon, number=compact badge. Default: 'label'.
propDescriptions.components: MarkdownComponents. Custom renderers; math({value, display}) opts into $…$/$$…$$ parsing. Renderer owns output and accessibility.
propDescriptions.contentAlign: 'start'|'center'. Prose alignment when contentWidth < container. Default: 'start'.
propDescriptions.contentWidth: number|string. Max width for prose (headings, paragraphs, lists). Tables/code unconstrained. Default: 680.
propDescriptions.headingLevelStart: Maps # to this heading level (1-6). Clamped to h6. Default: 1.
propDescriptions.inlinePlugins: MarkdownInlinePlugin[]. Regex matches in text nodes -> custom inline React elements. Skips inline/fenced code and math.
propDescriptions.isStreaming: Incremental parse + fade-in for streamed chunks. Default: false.
propDescriptions.onLinkClick: (href, event) => void|false. Return false prevents navigation. Link destinations follow the shared navigation rule (see Link href), and every data: link or image URL is also dropped; rejected ones render as text. A custom link renderer does not receive it.
propDescriptions.plugins: readonly MarkdownPluginEntry[]. Ordered syntax, immutable AST transforms, and typed extension renderers from createMarkdownPlugin(), plus first-party helpers such as createMarkdownHeadingLinks(). Default: omitted or empty.
propDescriptions.sources: Record<string, MarkdownSource>. Citation sources by ID. [id]/【id】 markers render as chips.
propDescriptions.xstyle: stylex.create() for layout (margins, sizing).
