bestPractices.description: Set headingLevelStart to match the page hierarchy, e.g. start at 3 if the markdown sits inside an h2 section.
Use contentWidth to keep prose at a readable line length in wide layouts.

Emphasis and strong pair as CommonMark specifies, so *see **bold** more* puts the bold inside the emphasis. ***text*** renders as strong around emphasis, the order RichText draws, and is announced as both. Emphasis nested more than 100 levels deep stays as written text.
Use plugins created by createMarkdownPlugin for reusable syntax, immutable AST transforms, and typed extension rendering. Keep the ordered list stable while its syntax configuration is unchanged.

To render a plugin node outside Markdown, as another surface showing the same document does, read what the plugin declares with getMarkdownPluginCapabilities (syntax and transform, nothing else), and render each parsed extension node with MarkdownPluginNodeRenderer from the client-only @astryxdesign/core/Markdown/plugin-renderer subpath. It presents the node exactly as Markdown does, fallbacks and failure reports included, with no element of its own.

Add markdownSoftBreaksPlugin when single line endings are meaningful. It matches remark-breaks for supported Markdown, including multiline link labels, while code and other opaque content stay unchanged.

Add markdownSourceLinesPlugin when a feature maps the rendered document back to Markdown source lines (find, highlights, review comments). Every block Markdown renders, nested blocks included, then carries data-source-line and data-source-line-end (1-based, inclusive); components block renderers receive sourceLines to place on their own element, and plugin renderers read node.position lines. Inline elements, table rows, and cells carry none. Without the plugin no line work runs.

Use createMarkdownTextTransform for prose matching; it preserves code, links, images, citations, math, and accepted extension syntax as protected contexts. Provide requiredSubstrings only when they conservatively cover every possible match.

Use createMarkdownFenceTransform for declared code-fence languages with semantic data. createNode returns an owned block extension node; its standard plugin renderer and toText own presentation. A claimed fence renders through that plugin even when components.code is supplied; components.code renders every unclaimed fence and is the fallback when the plugin renderer declines, throws, or suspends, and without it the accessible, copyable CodeBlock is that fallback.

Use createMarkdownSourceDecoration to attach non-visual metadata — search hits, review annotations — to the blocks a source range touches, and getMarkdownSourceDecorations to read it back in a later plugin. Decorations appear on the settled document rather than on partial streaming chunks, and never change rendering, copyable text, accessible names, ids, focus order, or navigation.

Import parseMarkdownAst or parseInlineAst from @astryxdesign/core/Markdown/parser when server or React Server Component code needs to run plugins against the canonical readonly tree. The parser and plugin subpaths have no use-client boundary. The Markdown component remains client-owned, so function-bearing plugin entries must not be passed across an RSC serialization boundary.

Use createMarkdownFrontmatter for typed document metadata. Its parse() method gives the host metadata directly; its plugin removes a complete leading block before rendering and withholds an unfinished block during streaming.

Import createMarkdownRemarkTransform from '@astryxdesign/core/Markdown/remark' only to reuse a synchronous transform-only Remark plugin; it stays out of every other bundle and unsupported behavior keeps the last valid document with one diagnostic.
Use inlinePlugins for prefixed identifiers, mentions, and other prose-only shorthand instead of preprocessing the markdown string.
Provide components.math only for documents that use dollar-delimited math; the renderer owns typesetting and accessible output.

Direct math parser calls use MathParseOptions and the explicit WithMath node unions; incremental calls also use createIncrementalState<true>() and IncrementalParseState<true>. Default calls keep the legacy unions.

Install createMarkdownHeadingLinks() through plugins to add all-depth stable IDs and inline trailing # copy buttons to built-in headings. useContainerReveal keeps each button hidden at fine-pointer rest and keyboard/touch reachable. Unmodified activation copies the canonical URL without navigation, hash mutation, or scrolling and shows a 1.5-second check; a failed copy shows a cross and the name "Failed to copy value to clipboard." for the same time and announces it once. Pass the same plugin entry to Markdown-derived Outline; use headingIdPrefix for multiple instances.
Use Markdown for hand-authored layouts; use Text and Heading directly when you control the content.
Do not pass plugins from a Server Component into Markdown; function-bearing entries cannot cross the client boundary. Create them in client code.
Do not rely on Markdown to sanitize custom, plugin, or math renderer output; each renderer owns its output and semantics.

## Getting Started

Install the package:

```bash
npm install @astryxdesign/core
```

Then import and use any component:

```tsx
import {Button} from '@astryxdesign/core/Button';
```

**Bold**, *italic*, and `inline code` all work.

props.description: The markdown string to render.
props.name: children

props.description: Display type. Markdown defaults to block. Use 'inline' for markdown spans embedded inside text.
props.name: display

props.description: Controls spacing between block-level elements.
props.name: density

props.description: The HTML heading level that markdown # maps to. Shifts all heading levels down to fit the surrounding page hierarchy. Levels exceeding h6 are clamped to h6.
props.name: headingLevelStart

props.description: Enables streaming mode; it uses incremental parsing and a smooth fade-in animation for chunk-by-chunk text delivery.
props.name: isStreaming

props.description: Handler for link clicks. Return false to prevent the default navigation behavior. Link destinations in the markdown follow the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop, and Markdown also rejects every data: URL in a link or an image: a rejected destination renders as plain text and never reaches this handler or a custom link renderer. A custom link renderer replaces the default link and does not receive this handler.
props.name: onLinkClick

props.description: Citation sources keyed by ID. When provided, [id] and 【id】 markers in the markdown that match a key are rendered as citation chips.
props.name: sources

props.description: How citations are displayed inline. 'label' shows a chip with source title, icon, and border. 'number' shows a compact numbered badge.
props.name: citationStyle

props.description: Max width for prose content (paragraphs, headings, lists, blockquotes). Tables and code blocks are unconstrained and can expand to the full container width. Use for readable line lengths in wide layouts.
props.name: contentWidth

props.description: Alignment of prose content within the container when contentWidth is narrower than the available space.
props.name: contentAlign

props.description: Ordered extensions created by createMarkdownPlugin(). Plugins may add bounded syntax, immutable typed AST transforms, and typed extension renderers. Use isMarkdownExtensionNode() to narrow extension data observed from other plugins. Renderer callbacks are pure; return a child component when hooks are needed. Omitted and empty lists preserve the released Markdown behavior.
props.name: plugins

props.description: Transforms regex matches in parsed text nodes into custom inline React elements. Use for prefixed identifiers, mentions, and other shorthand patterns. Inline code, fenced code blocks, and math are unaffected.
props.name: inlinePlugins

props.description: Opt-in autolinking of bare URLs and emails. 'gfm' applies GitHub-Flavored Markdown autolink-literal rules: bare https?://..., www...., <scheme:url>, <email>, and user@host all become links. Trailing sentence punctuation and unbalanced trailing close-parens are excluded; matches inside code spans, code blocks, existing links, and image alt text are skipped. Default behavior (option unset) is unchanged.
props.name: autolink

props.description: CodeBlock language values a fence may name, each imported on its own (e.g. graphql from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/graphql) or made with createCodeLanguage. A fence whose language word is one of a listed value's identifiers renders with it, ahead of a built-in; a diff-<identifier> fence takes the diff layer over it; a later entry wins. Pass the same list to RichTextEditor or RichTextView so read and edit match.
props.name: codeLanguages

props.description: Custom React component overrides for rendered Markdown elements (code, inlineCode, math, link, heading, paragraph, image, blockquote, hr, citation). Providing math enables `$…$` inline and `$$…$$` display parsing and receives `{value, display}`; omit it when dollar text should stay literal.
props.name: components

props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.
props.name: xstyle

props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.
props.name: className

props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.
props.name: style

props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.
props.name: data-testid

Inline elements, table rows, and cells carry none. Without the plugin no line work runs.

Use createMarkdownTextTransform for prose matching; it preserves code, links, images, citations, math, and accepted extension syntax as protected contexts. Provide requiredSubstrings only when they conservatively cover every possible match.

Use createMarkdownFenceTransform for declared code-fence languages with semantic data. createNode returns an owned block extension node; its standard plugin renderer and toText own presentation. A claimed fence renders through that plugin even when components.code is supplied; components.code renders every unclaimed fence and is the fallback when the plugin renderer declines, throws, or suspends, and without it the accessible, copyable CodeBlock is that fallback.

Use createMarkdownSourceDecoration to attach non-visual metadata — search hits, review annotations — to the blocks a source range touches, and getMarkdownSourceDecorations to read it back in a later plugin. Import parseMarkdownAst or parseInlineAst from @astryxdesign/core/Markdown/parser when server or React Server Component code needs to run plugins against the canonical readonly tree. The parser and plugin subpaths have no use-client boundary. The Markdown component remains client-owned, so function-bearing plugin entries must not be passed across an RSC serialization boundary.

Use decodeMarkdownCharacterReferences (from @astryxdesign/core/Markdown/parser or @astryxdesign/core/Markdown) to show text the way Markdown renders its character references: ©, ©, and © become ©, while unknown names and references without their semicolon stay as written. It decodes plain text and knows nothing of Markdown, so skip code and backslash-escaped references yourself. It uses the same table Markdown renders with.

Use createMarkdownFrontmatter for typed document metadata. Its parse() method gives the host metadata directly; its plugin removes a complete leading block before rendering and withholds an unfinished block during streaming.

Use inlinePlugins for prefixed identifiers, mentions, and other prose-only shorthand instead of preprocessing the markdown string.

The returned entry carries its validated namespace and URL base across compatible Core package copies. Each built-in heading keeps its incoming fragment ID and gains an inline trailing # copy button: it is hidden at fine-pointer rest through useContainerReveal, reveals on heading-row hover or keyboard focus, and stays visible under the hook’s coarse/touch semantics. The no-plugin path stays unchanged, and nested headings use the same depth-first identity projection as Markdown-derived Outline.

For multiple documents, create one heading-links plugin per document with headingIdPrefix and pass that same plugin to Markdown and useOutlineFromMarkdown. Use the same stable value for Markdown id when the root also needs a DOM id; permalinkBaseUrl may supply a safe caller-owned URL before the fragment.
Use Markdown for hand-authored layouts; use Text and Heading directly when you control the content.

Do not rely on Markdown to sanitize what a custom renderer, a plugin renderer, or components.math returns. Markdown passes them inert text and parsed nodes; each renderer owns its own output and its accessible semantics.

usage.description: Renders a markdown string as Astryx-styled components. Use Markdown for user-generated content, AI responses, and documentation; it handles headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and citations with consistent styling.

propDescriptions.fallback: side auto uses when surface is unmeasurable (SSR, first frame, background-image, which needs useImageMode sampling); ignored unless mode is auto
propDescriptions.mode: surface luminance context: dark for content over dark backgrounds (light text, white-tinted interactions), light for content over light backgrounds (dark text, black-tinted interactions), auto to decide from painted surface (none if ambient text already reads at 3:1, else better-reading side), off to turn off explicitly (element still renders, so children never remount)

bestPractices.description: Use for any content over dark background (image overlays, video scrims, dark cards) or other inverted surfaces like toasts/tooltips.
Prefer mode="auto" when surface color comes from a theme token; a token named "inverted" is not guaranteed to be; auto measures what was painted.
Pair w/ background color: MediaTheme flips token context but does NOT add background. Set backgroundColor on parent element.
Themes can customize components on media surfaces via onDark.components + onLight.components in defineTheme(). E.g. add border to ghost buttons on dark surfaces.
Use MediaTheme for app-level dark mode: use Theme w/ mode="dark"/mode="system" instead. MediaTheme is for local surface inversions, not page-wide color scheme.

usage.description: Token overrides for content on inverted surfaces: media overlays, scrims, toasts, tooltips. Base behavior flips color-scheme so all light-dark() tokens resolve to correct side; only a small set of tokens need explicit overrides beyond that. Themes can further customize component appearance on media surfaces via onDark/onLight in defineTheme(), w/ token overrides (e.g. "--color-accent": "#90CAF9") + component overrides (e.g. ghost buttons get border on dark surfaces).

children.children: Text and actions adapt to the dark media surface.

props.description: Surface luminance context: dark for content over dark backgrounds (light text, white-tinted interactions), light for content over light backgrounds (dark text, black-tinted interactions), auto to decide from the painted surface (no media context when the ambient text already reads on the surface at 3:1, otherwise the side that reads better), and off to turn it off explicitly. The element renders either way, so a surface can switch contexts without remounting children.
props.name: mode

props.description: Which side auto uses when the surface cannot be measured: during SSR, on the first client frame, and whenever the backdrop is not knowable from CSS, most often a background-image, whose pixels need sampling (useImageMode) rather than a computed style. Ignored unless mode is auto.
props.name: fallback

props.description: Content to render with inverted token context. Components inherit the correct colors automatically.
props.name: children

bestPractices.description: Use for any content placed over a dark background (image overlays, video scrims, dark cards) or other inverted surfaces like toasts and tooltips.

Prefer mode="auto" when the surface color comes from a theme token. A token named "inverted" is not guaranteed to be inverted, and auto measures what was actually painted instead of trusting the name. It can even decide that a surface needs no media context at all.
Pair with a background color: MediaTheme flips the token context but does not add a background. Set backgroundColor on the parent element.
Themes can customize components on media surfaces via onDark.components and onLight.components in defineTheme(). For example, add a border to ghost buttons on dark surfaces.
Use MediaTheme for app-level dark mode: use Theme with mode="dark" or mode="system" instead. MediaTheme is for local surface inversions, not page-wide color scheme.

usage.description: Provides token overrides for content rendered on inverted surfaces: media overlays, scrims, toasts, and tooltips. The base behavior flips color-scheme so all light-dark() tokens resolve to the correct side. Only a small set of tokens need explicit overrides beyond that. Themes can further customize component appearance on media surfaces via onDark/onLight in defineTheme(), with both token overrides (e.g. "--color-accent": "#90CAF9") and component overrides (e.g. ghost buttons get a border on dark surfaces).

props.description: Label text for accessibility.
props.name: label

props.description: Array of items: strings, objects with value/label/icon/disabled, dividers, or sections. An option may carry `action`: one node — an IconButton, a Button, a menu trigger — the caller renders and names. Once any option does, the popup is a grid whose rows pair the option with its action: Up/Down move rows, the inline-end arrow reaches the action, Enter fires it, pointer and touch press it directly, and pressing it never changes the selection.
props.name: options

props.description: Currently selected values.
props.name: value

props.description: Called when the selection changes. A creation (hasCreate) arrives with `{type: "create", query}` as the second argument and the query appended to value; the caller adds the matching option in that same update. Every other change passes no descriptor, so a one-argument handler keeps working.
props.name: onChange

props.description: Async action on change. Fires after onChange.
props.name: changeAction

props.description: Placeholder text shown when no value is selected.
props.name: placeholder

props.description: Size variant for the selector.
props.name: size

props.description: How to display selected items in the trigger.
props.name: triggerDisplay

props.description: Maximum badges to show before "+N". Only for triggerDisplay="badges".

props.name: selectAllLabel

props.description: Whether to show a search input for filtering options. As the user types, the match count (or "No results found") is announced to screen readers via a polite live region. The search field has built-in affordances: a leading magnifier icon and, once a query is typed, a trailing clear (✕) button that resets the query and returns focus to the input.
props.name: hasSearch

props.description: Placeholder text for the search input.
props.name: searchPlaceholder

props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when there are no options to show, and announced in a polite live region when the panel opens. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both. Not shown while isLoading.
props.name: emptyText

props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when a search query matches no options, and announced in a polite live region at the same time. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both.
props.name: emptySearchText

props.description: With hasSearch, offers a `Create "<query>"` row first in the list when the typed text equals no option label under the search’s case-insensitive matching. Picking it, or Enter with nothing highlighted, calls onChange with the query appended to value and a `{type: "create", query}` descriptor, then clears the search; the caller must add an option for the new value in that update. Nothing is offered while isLoading. Without hasSearch it warns in development and offers nothing.
props.name: hasCreate

props.description: Disables the selector.
props.name: isDisabled

props.description: Makes the selector read-only: the selected values stay visible, focusable, and included in form submission, and retain their combobox identity with aria-readonly. The selection surface, clear action, and disclosure indicator are removed. Unlike isDisabled, the control is not dimmed. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.
props.name: isReadOnly

props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders one hidden input per selected value, like a native multi-select.
props.name: htmlName

props.description: Explains why the selector is disabled. With isDisabled, shows the reason as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus of the trigger, which stays focusable (aria-disabled) like every disabled selector; activation stays blocked. Use this instead of wrapping a disabled MultiSelector in Tooltip.

props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.
props.name: isLabelHidden

props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.description: Marks the field as optional.

props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.description: Shows a loading spinner in the trigger.

props.description: Validation status with an optional message.

bestPractices.description: Use for a moderate, finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.
Enable search filtering when the list exceeds ~15 options.
Use renderOption for custom option rows; the checkbox affordance remains owned by MultiSelector.
Enable select-all when most users will want all or nearly all options selected.
Use inside InputGroup only when the control needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface; prefer count or labels trigger display so the group stays single-line.

Use variant="secondary" when a multi-selector sits beside secondary buttons or segmented controls, and variant="ghost" when it sits beside ghost buttons. If validation status is needed there, prefer statusVariant="tooltip" so the toolbar height stays compact.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the multi-selector should become a bottom sheet on compact touch screens.
Use for single-value selection; use Selector instead.
Show more than ~20 options without enabling search.
Wrap a disabled MultiSelector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the trigger itself.

bestPractices.description: Pass NavHeadingMenu as the menu prop of SideNavHeading or TopNavHeading. Where the heading closes on a choice, choosing an enabled item runs its onClick or link and closes the menu.

NavHeadingMenu follows the keyboard model of the WAI-ARIA APG Menu pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/): a menu of menuitem rows. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move one row and wrap, Home and End go to the first and last row, typing a character moves to the matching row, Enter or Space activates the row, and Escape closes the heading menu where the heading supplies a close action.
Give a NavHeadingMenu used on its own an aria-label. The menu has no accessible name unless you pass one.

Remove a destination the user cannot use right now when knowing it exists helps them. Set isDisabled instead: the row stays reachable by the arrow keys and typeahead, is announced as disabled, and does nothing when chosen.
Put other interactive controls in the menu. The arrow keys move only between NavHeadingMenuItem rows, so another control is skipped.

propDescriptions.entryErrorBehavior: 'complete'|'blur-or-enter': when the field's own rejection shows (not when validation runs; not React Aria validationBehavior; never changes status). A typed number is complete only at Enter/blur, so both values behave the same: message, aria-invalid, styling, announcement and onEntryErrorChange report wait for Enter/blur; valid or emptied text clears at once. Default: nearest FormLayout defaultEntryErrorBehavior, else complete

propDescriptions.hasNumberSteppers: Show increment + decrement buttons on fine pointers; hidden on coarse pointers. Defaults to false.
propDescriptions.htmlName: HTML name for form submissions; while blur keeps rejected text, posts the committed number until an edit or a new value.
propDescriptions.isLabelHidden: Visually hide label (still accessible to screen readers).
propDescriptions.isReadOnly: Read-only: value visible + still submits, but not editable. Unlike isDisabled: not dimmed.

propDescriptions.label: Label text (always rendered for accessibility).

propDescriptions.onChange: Callback when a valid text edit commits on blur/Enter, or a step/clear control changes the value.
propDescriptions.onEntryErrorChange: (error|null) on each typed-rejection change, starting only at Enter/blur: kind 'unreadable'|'fractional' (isIntegerOnly)|'outOfRange' (min > max), text, value (fractional/outOfRange); also on an edit to valid/empty, new value/min/max/isIntegerOnly, disable; never twice for one rejection; null on unmount mid-rejection; word it via an error status w/ message

propDescriptions.status: Validation status w/ optional message; nothing shows while typing; at Enter/blur, unreadable text, a fraction when isIntegerOnly, or any number while min > max stays w/ the field's own error message in place of status, unless status is an error w/ message (still announced + aria-invalid); warning/success never hide it; out-of-range numbers clamp.

props.description: Validation status with optional message. Typing never shows a rejection: a typed number is complete only at commit. When Enter or blur meets text that is not a number, a fraction in an integer-only field, or any number while min is above max, the text stays in the field and the field shows its own error message in place of status. An error status with a message shows instead of that message, and the rejection is still announced and marks the field invalid. A warning or success status, or an error status without a message, never replaces it. A number outside an ordinary range clamps instead.
props.name: status

props.description: Called each time the field's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. A rejection starts only at Enter or blur. kind is 'unreadable' (text that is not a number), 'fractional' (a fraction when isIntegerOnly), or 'outOfRange' (any number while min is above max); text is the typed text; value is the number it names, for 'fractional' and 'outOfRange'. It also runs when an edit makes the text valid or empty, when a new value, min, max, or isIntegerOnly changes or ends the rejection, and when disabling the field drops the text, and never twice for the same rejection; it reports null when the field unmounts while a rejection stands. Pass an error status with a message to word the rejection yourself.
props.name: onEntryErrorChange
props.type: (error: {kind: 'unreadable' | 'fractional' | 'outOfRange', text: string, value?: number} | null) => void

props.description: When the field shows its own entry error: typed text it rejects, as onEntryErrorChange reports it. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. A typed number is complete only at Enter or blur, so 'complete' and 'blur-or-enter' behave the same: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report appear together at Enter or blur, never while a person types, and an edit that makes the text valid or empty clears the error at once. Set it to match the other fields of a form; the field's own value wins over the nearest FormLayout's defaultEntryErrorBehavior.
props.name: entryErrorBehavior

props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

dense.description: Document outline/table-of-contents nav with sliding indicator track. Flat items array {id,label,level}; anchor links; density variant (default/compact); uncontrolled scroll-spy by scroll position (last heading past its resting line = offset + its own scroll-margin-top; first item at top, last at bottom); controlled with activeId; smooth-scroll on click that pins the active item until the next manual scroll. Each link is a Tab stop; Enter/Space activate; no arrow/Home/End movement. onNavigateStart/onNavigateEnd fire around the scroll. Scroll scoping via offset / scrollContainerRef / hasScrollOnClick.

bestPractices.description: Place pagination below the content it controls so users see results before navigating.
Use the pages variant for data tables where users need to jump to a specific page.
Use the count variant with a page size selector when users need to control how many items they see at once.
Use the dots variant for carousels and walkthroughs where the total is small and position matters more than a number.

Pass getPageHref when each page has its own URL, so a page opens in a new tab and its address can be copied.
Give each Pagination a distinct label when a page has more than one, so screen-reader users can tell the navigation landmarks apart.

Use the dots variant for more than about 10 pages; the dots become too small to be useful.
Place pagination above the content; users expect it at the bottom.

Provide a clear way to close: either by clicking outside or with an explicit close button.

props.description: How the field presents filter editing. adaptive (the default) uses the bottom sheet on compact touch screens and the popover otherwise, resolved the same way Selector resolves it; the server render and the hydrating render are the popover. popover is the tokenizer field with its typeahead and the editor popover on every device. bottom-sheet makes the whole field, on every device, one trigger showing display-only filter tokens: it opens a Filters sheet listing the filters as rows that edit or remove a filter, with Add filter, Done, and Clear all (which asks first and keeps read-only filters); an Add filter sheet with the fields (or the content search with inline suggestions) opens above it, and a value step that stages operator → value and confirms from its footer opens above that. Choose `inline`, `block`, or `both` from content intent; the component maps the logical axes through writing mode and direction.
Keep the default `overscroll="allow"` for nested areas unless the interaction deliberately needs containment.

Use `useScrollableArea` instead when a component already owns both a viewport and a suitable content box, or when children must remain direct flex/grid items or retain a definite percentage block-size basis.

ScrollableArea owns one normal block content box with a 100% minimum size. Inline and both-axis modes use max-content inline sizing, so intrinsic inline layout is intentionally wider than the viewport.

Set `isFullBleed` only when the viewport itself should reach an ancestor container edge; it is off by default.
Set `stickyContainment="always"` only when a fitting viewport should intentionally remain a Sticky boundary.
Hide the native scrollbar without another visible and operable overflow affordance.

usage.description: A segmented button group that allows users to make a single selection from a small set of mutually exclusive options. Use SegmentedControl when all options should be visible at once and the selection controls a value or mode, not page navigation. Under a finger, on a touch device (a coarse primary pointer), the selection slides to the new segment, whether a tap, an arrow key or a new value moved it; with Reduce Motion nothing travels: the old selection fades out as the new one fades in. There, pressing the selected segment lifts it, and dragging it carries the selection along with the selected label’s colour following it, and the segment under the finger is chosen when it lets go; a tap selects through the browser’s click; a pressed unselected segment shows the shared pressed overlay, and nothing dims. A drag that drifts off the control still chooses by its position along it. Going back to the selected segment, or Escape, changes nothing. With a mouse or a pen every change, a click included, slides on the theme’s duration and easing, and dragging the selected segment carries it as a finger does.

usage.description: A dropdown selector for choosing a single value from a list of options. Supports labels, validation, descriptions, and required/optional states. Use it in forms and settings when presenting a moderate number of options. Keyboard typeahead matches a native select: typing on the focused closed trigger selects the matching option directly, repeated presses cycle through options sharing a first letter, and spaces count as match characters ("new y" reaches "New York"). With the menu open, typing moves the highlight and Enter commits. With hasSearch, typing on the closed trigger opens the popup and seeds the search input.

bestPractices.description: Provide a visible label so users understand what they are selecting.
Use sections and dividers to organize options when the list exceeds ~8 items.
Use renderOption for custom option rows. Do not pass SelectorOption directly as JSX children.
Set a meaningful placeholder that hints at the expected selection (e.g. "Choose a country" not "Select...").
Use inside InputGroup only when the selector needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface.

Use variant="secondary" when a selector sits in a nav or toolbar beside secondary buttons or a segmented control, so it shares their treatment instead of reading as a form field. Use variant="ghost" when a selector sits in a toolbar with ghost buttons. If validation status is needed there, prefer statusVariant="tooltip" so the toolbar height stays compact.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the selector should become a bottom sheet on compact touch screens.
Use for action menus; use Dropdown Menu for triggering commands or navigation.
Use when there are only two options; use a SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Use Selector for navigation; links should be links, not dropdown options.
Use for yes/no or on/off choices; use Switch or CheckboxInput instead.
Put more than ~20 options without sections; consider Typeahead for large lists.
Wrap a disabled Selector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the trigger itself.

usage.description: A dropdown selector for choosing a single value from a list of options. Supports labels, validation, descriptions, and required/optional states. Mark the current page with isSelected: it sets aria-current="page", so the current destination is announced rather than carried by color alone.

SideNav renders a navigation landmark, and a collapsible item follows the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/): the toggle carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the group it owns is inert while collapsed. Keep item labels short; they name icon-only items unless a meaningful aria-label supplies more context.

While the nav is collapsed, an item with children shows them in a submenu flyout. On a device that can hover, pointing at the item opens it after a short delay and moving away closes it; a flyout opened by clicking stays open until it is dismissed. On touch, it opens on tap. Do not put an action in there that has no other route to it.
Include a SideNavHeading when a TopNav is already providing app identity; this duplicates branding.
Use for filtering content; use tabs or filter buttons instead.

usage.description: A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it.

usage.description: A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it.

usage.description: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser’s click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse.

bestPractices.description: Use density and divider variants to match the information density and scanning needs of your data.
Compose cells via renderCell w/ Text, StatusDot, Avatar. Pair StatusDot w/ Text; solid Badge only for the rare cell that needs attention.

Children mode: wrap rows in TableHeader/TableBody/TableFooter. <table> cannot hold a <tr> directly; the parser adds an implied <tbody> for SSR markup, React does not on the client, so unwrapped rows mismatch on hydration.
Omitted width = equal flex w/ compact 60px readability floor. Per-column floor: proportional(1, {minWidth}). Weighted: proportional(n). Fixed: pixel(). Table scrolls when combined floors do not fit.
Data-driven API is RSC-safe: proportional(), pixel(), column defs w/o function props work in Server Components. renderCell (any function prop) requires a "use client" wrapper.
Row open/click: no row-click prop. Put a Link or Button in the main cell via renderCell. <tr> onClick alone is not keyboard or screen-reader reachable. renderCell turns windowing off (full render).
Filtered/searched data can be empty: set emptyState (e.g. EmptyState + "Clear filters" Button).

Long tokens (IDs, URLs) under explicit `columns` break inside the token when the column is narrower (sized from definitions, not content). Keep them whole w/ proportional(1, {minWidth}) or pixel() wide enough, or children mode (columns follow content).

With `columns`: floors (`minWidth`, `pixel()`) are minimums; content never widens a column, except a windowed numbering column (children mode sizes to content). Floors wider than the screen = sideways scroll on a phone; columns past the edge hidden until a swipe.

Phone-first page: below a breakpoint show the data as a List instead of the Table. Render both; switch w/ a StyleX `display` rule under `@media (not (min-width: 768px))` (theme `md` breakpoint; CSS: right layout at first paint, no script). Not `useMediaQuery` (only after script).

Put a control (button, link, input) in a sortable column header: the Sort control wraps the header, so the nested control is inoperable for assistive technology. Keep header controls on unsortable columns.
Use a table for data without consistent columns. Use a list or card layout for heterogeneous content.
Enable every plugin at once. Add only the features your use case requires to keep the interface focused.
Rely on the 60px omitted-width floor for a text-heavy column that needs more room; set proportional(1, {minWidth}) on it instead.

It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead.

props.description: Column definitions: each column has {key, header, width?, align?, renderCell?}, and Table has no onRowClick prop; the supported way to open a dialog, side panel or detail page from a row is a Link or Button in the row's main cell (renderCell) that opens it, and to show a row's details inline on a click anywhere on it, use useTableRowExpansion with hasRowClickExpansion; on a phone, column floors wider than the screen scroll sideways, so for a phone-first page also render one List with `hasDividers` (not a Card per item) and switch with a StyleX `display` rule under `@media` (Best practices). The `header` field sets the column heading text. If omitted, columns are auto-generated from data object keys. The `width` field is typed as `ColumnWidth` (not a number); use `proportional(n)` or `pixel(n)` helpers imported from `@astryxdesign/core/Table`. Omitting `width` keeps an equal flexible share with a compact 60px readability floor. To give one column a different floor, set `width: proportional(1, {minWidth: 80})`; its `minWidth` replaces the 60px floor for that column. Example: `width: pixel(120)` for 120px fixed, `width: proportional(1)` for a flexible column with a 120px default minimum.

A theme restyles either stripe of a data-driven table through the `table-row` target's `parity` (odd or even); every row a striped table may stripe (body and footer rows, not the header row) carries the `striped` state. A pinned column (`useTableStickyColumns`) follows the row's stripe.

props.description: How cell text behaves when it exceeds the column width. 'wrap' lets text wrap and the row grow taller; 'truncate' clips with an ellipsis (default-rendered cells show a tooltip on hover when truncated). Header cells follow the same mode: under 'wrap' a long heading wraps in a data-driven table, and in children mode its column grows to keep it on one line. When you pass `columns`, a data-driven table sizes them from their definitions, not their content, so under 'wrap' a token longer than its column, such as a code identifier or a URL, breaks inside the token where the line ends. To keep such tokens whole, give that column a floor that fits them, or compose the table in children mode, whose columns follow their content.

props.description: Geometry-only capability from useTableRowsVirtualization or useTableColumnsVirtualization, or a list with at most one of each; any other list renders without windowing. useTableColumnsVirtualization({initialViewportWidth}) mounts only the unpinned columns near the viewport. useTableRowsVirtualization({rowHeight, initialViewportHeight}) takes sizes that are both positive finite CSS pixels; the Table scrolls inside the height its parent gives it, and initialViewportHeight only sizes the first window. Give the Table's parent a height, fixed or relative, or a flex child, so windowing can bound the rows; with no height every row renders. Pass complete flat data and an explicit idKey. Default text truncates; custom renderers, wrapping, structural plugins, incompatible offsets, invalid identity or unrepresentable geometry use full rendering. Logical row positions include the header.
props.name: virtualization

props.description: Named plugins: the objects that the useTable* hooks return, or your own TablePlugin<T> (import the type from @astryxdesign/core/Table), an object of optional transform functions. When the table renders, Table calls transformColumns, transformTable, transformHeaderCell for each header cell, transformHeaderRow, transformScrollWrapper, and then transformTableContext in reverse plugin order, so the first plugin wraps outermost. With column virtualization, transformHeaderCell and transformHeaderRow run after transformScrollWrapper and transformTableContext, because the header renders inside the column window. Then, as each body row renders, Table calls transformBodyRow for that row and then transformBodyCell for each of its cells. Their arguments and results: transformColumns(columns) adds, removes, or reorders columns; transformTable(props) changes the <table> props; transformHeaderCell(props, column, columnIndex, columns) changes a <th>, with slots before, content, after, overlay, and below; transformHeaderRow(props) changes the header <tr>; transformBodyCell(props, column, item, columnIndex, columns, context) changes a <td>; transformBodyRow(props, item, index, context) changes a body <tr>, and can add afterRow content below the row; transformScrollWrapper(props, context) changes the scroll region and can add beforeTable or afterTable content; transformTableContext(children) wraps the table in providers. The element transforms (table, header row, header cell, body row, body cell, scroll wrapper) receive {htmlProps, xstyle, ...} and must return the same shape, with the earlier values kept. Header and body cell transforms can also append contextMenuActions for a right-click menu. A plugin that has transformBodyRow or transformBodyCell and keeps one row per data item must set rowModel: 'flat'; without it, row virtualization uses full rendering and Table ignores plugin loading state (renderState). Keep each plugin object stable (create it in useMemo): a new object on each render renders all rows again. Plugins with the first-party names columnSettings, sort, tree, selection, and pagination run in that order; other names run after them, in record order.
props.name: plugins

props.description: ARIA row index (1-based) for the first rendered body row. The row ordinal is an accessibility concern independent of any visible index column, so setting this (or rowCount) makes the table emit aria-rowindex on body rows and aria-rowcount on the table. For a paginated/windowed view, pass the offset of the first visible row (e.g. (page - 1) * pageSize + 1) so aria-rowindex reflects position in the full dataset. Data-driven mode only.
props.name: rowIndexStart

props.description: Total number of body rows across all pages/windows, used for aria-rowcount so assistive tech can announce "row X of Y" against the full dataset. bestPractices.description: Use density and divider variants to match the information density and scanning needs of your data.
Compose rich cell content with Astryx components like Text, StatusDot, and Avatar via renderCell. Pair a StatusDot with Text, and keep a solid Badge for the rare cell that needs attention.

Do not put a control (a button, link, or input) in the header of a sortable column. The Sort control wraps the whole header, so the control nests inside it and assistive technology cannot operate it. Keep header controls on columns that are not sortable.

In children mode, put every row inside TableHeader, TableBody, or TableFooter. <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly: the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup and React does not on the client, so unwrapped rows mismatch on hydration.

Omit width for equal flexible columns with a compact 60px readability floor. Give one column its own floor with proportional(1, {minWidth}), weight columns with proportional(n), and fix widths with pixel(); the Table scroll region activates when the combined floors no longer fit.

Use the data-driven API from React Server Components: proportional(), pixel(), and column definitions without function props are server-safe. Columns using renderCell (or any function prop) need the table wrapped in a "use client" component, since functions cannot cross the server-client boundary.

To open a row (go to a detail page, open a side panel), put a Link or a Button in the row's main cell with renderCell. Table has no row-click prop. A click handler on the <tr> cannot be reached with the keyboard or a screen reader, so do not use it as the only way to open a row. A renderCell column makes a windowed Table (virtualization) render every row.
When filters or a search can leave no rows, set emptyState to say so and offer a way out, for example an EmptyState with a "Clear filters" Button.

Keep long tokens such as code identifiers whole. When you pass `columns`, a data-driven table sizes them from their definitions, not their content, so a token that does not fit its column breaks inside the token. Give that column proportional(1, {minWidth}) or pixel() wide enough for the token, or compose the table in children mode, whose columns follow their content.

When you pass `columns`, floors set with `minWidth` or `pixel()` are minimums and cell content never widens a column, except that a windowed table’s numbering column fits its largest number (only children mode sizes columns to content). When the floors add up to more than the screen, the table scrolls sideways on a phone: the columns past the edge stay out of sight until the reader swipes.

For a page read mostly on phones, show the data as a List below a breakpoint instead of a wide table. Render both the List and the Table, and switch them with a StyleX `display` rule, for example `display: {default: 'none', '@media (not (min-width: 768px))': 'block'}` on the List’s wrapper and the reverse on the Table’s, below the theme’s `md` breakpoint (768px by default, or your theme’s own `md`). CSS picks the layout in the first paint and without script; `useMediaQuery` picks it only after the page’s script runs.
Use a table for data without consistent columns. Use a list or card layout for heterogeneous content.
Put a solid Badge (success, warning, error, info) in every cell of a column. The repeated fills compete with the data; pair a StatusDot with Text instead.
Enable every plugin at once. Add only the features your use case requires to keep the interface focused.
Rely on the 60px omitted-width floor when a text-heavy column needs more room; set proportional(1, {minWidth}) on that column instead.

props.description: Maximum number of characters allowed, counted as user-perceived characters: an emoji or flag sequence counts as one. When set, a character counter (current/max) is displayed inside the input container, anchored to the bottom-right beneath the text. Does not enforce the limit natively; when exceeded the counter turns red and shows a warning icon (a non-color cue), and screen-reader users hear the remaining/over-limit count announced. Consumers validating the limit should count with characterCount (exported from the package) so enforcement matches the displayed count.

props.description: The native `maxlength` attribute: the browser stops typing past this many UTF-16 code units (an emoji can take two or more). It is separate from `maxLength`, the soft counter of user-perceived characters: it works without the counter, and it neither shows nor changes the counter. It can stop typing before the counter reaches its limit. TextArea adds no truncation or validation of its own, so a longer controlled value stays as set. The attribute is in the server-rendered HTML, so it applies before hydration. Validate on the server too: the browser limit does not bind requests that skip the UI.

bestPractices.description: Provide a visible label so users know what to enter. If the label must be hidden, set isLabelHidden with a descriptive label for screen readers.
Set maxLength with a character counter when there is a defined limit; it helps users stay within bounds before they submit.
Keep Return a line break in a multi-line field. Relabel it with enterKeyHint (send, done) only when your own Enter handling does what the label says.
Use the status prop to surface validation feedback inline: show success when input is valid, warning for soft limits, and error for hard failures.
Add a description or placeholder to clarify expected content, like "Describe the issue in detail," but never rely on placeholder alone as the only label.
Avoid using TextArea for short, single-line values like names or emails; use TextInput instead.
Don't rely solely on placeholder text to communicate the purpose of the field; placeholders disappear on focus and are not accessible labels.
Don't show a status message without also setting the status type; the colored border and icon are what draw the user's attention to the message.
Don't wrap a disabled TextArea in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

bestPractices.description: Always provide a visible label so users know what the field is for. Only hide the label when surrounding context makes it obvious, like a search bar with a magnifying-glass icon.
Use validation status with a message to explain what went wrong: "Email must include @" is better than just turning the border red.
Size the input to match the expected content length so users can gauge how much to type: small for zip codes, medium for names, large for URLs.
Add a clear button for search and filter inputs so users can quickly reset without selecting all text.

Tell a touch keyboard what the field holds: `type="email"`, `"tel"` or `"url"` for those values, `inputMode="numeric"` for digits that are not a number (a one-time code), `enterKeyHint` for what Return does (Search, Send, Next), and `autoComplete` so AutoFill can fill it.
Don't use placeholder text as a replacement for a label; placeholders disappear on focus and are not reliably read by screen readers.
Don't use TextInput for multi-line content like comments or descriptions; use TextArea instead.
Don't mark every field as required; only flag mandatory fields so users are not overwhelmed by validation errors.
Don't wrap a disabled TextInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

propDescriptions.min: Min selectable time in ISO format. Out-of-range rejected.

propDescriptions.presentation: picker surface: 'adaptive-native' (default) = typed field fine / browser/OS coarse (hasSeconds or increment!=1 retains typed); 'native' = browser/OS always, no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' = typed fine / Astryx wheel sheet coarse; 'bottom-sheet' = sheet always; 'text-input'/'popover' = typed field only.

Use status prop for inline validation errors.

When unset, follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle: en-US reads 12-hour, en-GB and de-DE read 24-hour. To honor a person's own preference, pass it on the locale tag (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than per field.

'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's typed field on a fine pointer and the browser/OS input type=time on a coarse pointer — except hasSeconds or increment other than 1, which retain the typed field because iOS has no seconds wheel and treats step as validation rather than picker cadence; 'native' always uses the browser/OS control with no Astryx fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses the typed field on a fine pointer and Astryx's bottom-sheet time wheels on a coarse pointer; 'bottom-sheet' forces the wheels on every pointer; 'text-input' (like 'popover', which has no distinct TimeInput surface) keeps only the typed field. Native mode forwards min/max and enforces them on commit. hourFormat formats the closed value; the open OS picker follows the device locale.

props.description: Status indicator that colors the border and displays an icon. When a message is provided it is rendered below the input. A typed time the field rejects, and a native edit outside min or max, show the field's own error message instead; an error status with a message shows in its place, and the rejection is still announced. A warning or success never replaces a rejection.
props.name: status

props.description: Called each time the field's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. kind is 'unreadable' (text that is not a time) or 'outOfRange' (a time before min or after max); text is the typed text; value is the ISO time the text names, for 'outOfRange'. Under entryErrorBehavior 'complete', a rejection shows once the typed time is complete (in 12-hour text, with its day period unless the hour reads 0 or 13–23), or at Enter or blur; under 'blur-or-enter', only at Enter or blur. Rejected text stays in the field. It also runs when a new min, max, or value, or disabling the field, changes the rejection, never twice for the same rejection, and with null when the field unmounts while a rejection stands. The native and bottom-sheet surfaces take no typed text, so they never report.
props.name: onEntryErrorChange
props.type: (error: {kind: 'unreadable' | 'outOfRange', text: string, value?: ISOTimeString} | null) => void

props.description: When the field shows its own entry error: a typed time it rejects, as onEntryErrorChange reports it, or a native edit outside min or max. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. 'complete' shows a complete typed time outside min or max, and a native edit outside them, at once, and other rejected text at Enter or blur. 'blur-or-enter' holds every rejection until Enter or blur: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report then appear together. Under both values, an edit the field accepts or empties clears the error at once; under 'blur-or-enter', an edit that leaves the entry wrong keeps the shown error until the next Enter or blur. The field's own value wins over the nearest FormLayout's defaultEntryErrorBehavior.
props.name: entryErrorBehavior

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the time input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after TimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Set min and max constraints when the context has a valid range, like business hours or event windows, so users cannot submit an out-of-bounds time.
Provide a description or placeholder that hints at the expected format or purpose, like "Business hours: 9 AM – 5 PM".
Use the status prop to surface validation errors inline: show a message like "Time must be during business hours" so users know exactly what to fix.
Enable hasClear when the field is optional, so users can remove a previously selected time.
Place TimeInput inside InputGroup when the time needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon, like a start/end label or timezone marker.
Don't use TimeInput for combined date-and-time selection; pair it with a separate DateInput instead.
Don't hide the label; even when space is tight, keep the label visible or provide a description so the purpose is clear.
Wrap a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

usage.description: Timestamp formats a date or time into readable text. Use for creation dates, update times, or schedules; relative for recency, absolute for precision, auto to switch automatically.

props.description: The date/time to display. Accepts Unix timestamps (seconds) or ISO 8601 strings.
props.name: value

props.description: Display format. 'relative' uses the locale's native long relative-time wording ('2 hours ago' in English), 'relative_short' uses its narrow pattern ('2h ago' in English) for compact surfaces, 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2025', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2025', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2025', 'date_time' shows 'Mar 21, 2025, 2:51 PM', 'time' shows '2:51 PM', 'system_*' variants use ISO-style formatting, 'unix_seconds' shows the Unix time in whole seconds since the epoch (an absolute, zone-independent value), 'auto' switches from relative to date_time based on recency. Absolute formats never read the current time. 'relative', 'relative_short' and 'auto' read it on the client only: a server render or static prerender shows the full date and time in UTC, labelled, and the client switches to the format's normal output after hydration. Date-bearing formats ('date', 'date_long', 'date_weekday', 'date_time', and the full date in the hover card and the accessible name) use the InternationalizationProvider calendar, such as calendar="persian"; 'time', the relative formats, 'system_*', and 'unix_seconds' do not change.
props.name: format

props.description: IANA time zone the absolute formats render in, such as 'UTC' or 'America/Los_Angeles'. Omit (or pass 'local') for the viewer's own zone. An explicit zone renders identically on the server and the client, so it is the way to show an absolute time without a hydration mismatch; relative formats' visible text ignores it, while configured tooltipEntries rows still follow it. An unknown identifier warns once in development and falls back to the viewer's zone.

props.description: Threshold in seconds for 'auto' format to switch from relative to date_time.
props.name: autoThreshold

props.description: Whether to show a copyable hover card with the full date/time on hover or keyboard focus. Applies to relative timestamps and to any format once tooltipEntries is configured.

props.description: Lines to show on hover, so one instant can be read (and optionally copied) in several time zones and/or formats at once. Each entry is one line, in the order given. An entry without timezoneID follows the Timestamp timezoneID when set, else the viewer's zone; 'local' always means the viewer's zone; format defaults to the full absolute style and also accepts 'full' alongside every non-relative TimestampFormat. Rows are read-only unless they set isCopyable (default false); copyable rows show a copy button in a dedicated trailing action column so buttons align, and the column is only present when some row is copyable. With no entries the card shows a single default row with the full absolute time, which is copyable. Configuring entries also attaches the surface to absolute formats, which otherwise have none.

bestPractices.description: Use the auto format in feeds and lists so recent items show "2 hours ago" and older items show the full date automatically.
Keep formatting consistent within the same list or table; mixing relative and absolute timestamps in the same column confuses scanning.
Enable isTimezoneShown when the audience spans multiple time zones, like a global team calendar or audit log.
Use tooltipEntries when readers must compare zones, such as an incident log where the reader's time and the event's origin zone both matter.

Pass timezoneID when an absolute time must read the same for every viewer and on the server, like an incident log timestamp or anything server-rendered; without it the server markup depends on the server zone.
Label every entry once a tooltip shows more than one zone; a bare abbreviation is not always recognizable (Tokyo renders as "GMT+9", not "JST").
Use isLive for active dashboards or real-time feeds so the relative time stays accurate without a page refresh.

Reach for tooltipEntries when readers need to grab an exact value: an incident log or deploy record where someone pastes the UTC time or Unix seconds elsewhere; configuring entries turns the hover into copy-to-clipboard rows.
Don't display raw Unix timestamps or ISO strings to users; always pass them through Timestamp to get a human-readable format.
Avoid system_date or system_time formats in user-facing UI; they are meant for developer tools, logs, and machine-readable contexts.
Don't disable the hover card on relative timestamps; users expect to hover for the full date when they see "3 hours ago".
Don't stack many zones into one card; it is capped at 300px wide and long labelled lines wrap. Two or three entries read well.

Don't pass a fixed-offset abbreviation like "EST" as timezoneID; it is a valid identifier but never observes daylight saving, so it reads an hour wrong for half the year. Use the region id, "America/New_York".

Use where user needs feedback not decisions: saves, deletes, status changes. useToast() hook for production (safe-area positioning, responsive message wrapping, stacking, auto-dismiss, dedup via ToastViewport). Enters, exits, or swipe-dismisses toward configured edge; touch is claimed only after dominant edge-directed intent; swipe reports manual. Pen uses the direct-contact gesture; mouse drag stays off to preserve text selection and the close control remains available. Set isAutoHide false explicitly for must-remain actions/messages. Toast renders inline for previews/docs/static showcases. Host data-* attrs on Toast reach the toast element; role, live-region, theme attrs stay owned.

props.description: Replaces the content of this toast's card with your own layout. Astryx keeps the card, its astryx-toast theme target and auto-hide behavior (inside a ToastViewport the viewport announces the toast, over a modal too, and the card itself is not a live region), then hands the renderer the message, endContent, resolved toast settings and a dismiss callback. The custom renderer owns every control in its layout: compose the control you want and call dismiss from it. Astryx does not inject a fallback close into custom content. Per-toast: an app shares one layout by wrapping useToast and passing it on every call, while a toast raised by library code that never passes it renders as an ordinary Astryx toast. The argument is {body, endContent, type, isAutoHide, autoHideDuration, dismiss}, where type is 'info' | 'error'.

bestPractices.description: Keep messages short: only a few words that tell the user what happened, like "Changes saved" or "Message sent".
Add a short undo action in the endContent slot for reversible operations. Set isAutoHide to false when the action must remain available.
Pass useToast()'s uniqueID option to deduplicate toasts that fire from repeated actions, like clicking a save button multiple times.
Use error type for failures that need attention but not immediate action; it persists until dismissed so the user won't miss it.
Don't use a toast for critical errors that block the user. Use Banner for persistent, in-context messaging that requires acknowledgment.
Don't put long or multi-line content in a toast; it disappears after 5 seconds and the user may not finish reading.
Don't show form validation errors as toasts. Use inline field validation so the user can see exactly which field needs fixing.

usage.description:
Toast shows a brief, non-blocking notification to confirm an action or present temporary information; show one with `const showToast = useToast()`, which needs no provider or mounted ToastViewport: inside LayerProvider (or a ToastViewport) it uses that viewport, and otherwise the first toast mounts a fallback viewport on document.body with a development warning. Use it for scenarios where the user needs feedback but not a decision, such as saving, deleting, or changing a status.

For production use, prefer the `useToast()` hook; it handles positioning, stacking, auto-dismiss, and deduplication via `ToastViewport`. Only the viewport announces a toast: a `Toast` rendered on its own, as in a preview, is not a live region and announces nothing. Toasts stay within viewport and safe-area gutters, wrap long message content, and enter, exit, or swipe-dismiss toward their configured top or bottom edge. The vertical swipe uses the same spatial model as placement motion: top Toasts leave upward and bottom Toasts leave downward. Swipe waits for dominant edge-directed intent before cancelling native touch movement and reports the existing manual dismissal reason. Pen is supported as direct-contact input; mouse drag is excluded to avoid conflicting with desktop text selection, where the visible close control remains available. Set `isAutoHide: false` explicitly when an action or message must remain available. The `Toast` component renders the visual toast element inline and is useful for previews, documentation, and static showcases where the viewport lifecycle is not needed. Host `data-*` attributes on `Toast` reach the toast element; its role, live-region attributes, and theme attributes stay component-owned.

returnDescriptions.animatedLayout: opaque handle, no members; pass to a component's animatedLayout prop.

bestPractices.description: One handle per area, shared by its size-changing components.
Pass the ScrollableArea ref as containerRef; it does not register itself.
Wrap following content in an extra element to make it move.
Animate height yourself alongside it.

usage.description: One handle per scroll container/panel, passed to every component in it whose size changes. Content after a change (Astryx or app elements) glides; no opt-in per element. Omit the handle to keep the jump.

params.description: The area the glide stays inside: the ref you already give your scroll container or panel. A ScrollableArea ref reaches its native scroll viewport, so pass that.
params.name: options.containerRef

returns.description: An opaque handle with no public members. Pass it to the animatedLayout prop of a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible.
returns.name: animatedLayout
