Pass the ref you already give ScrollableArea as containerRef; ScrollableArea does not register itself.
Wrap the content after a disclosure in an extra element to make it move; everything after the change inside the container moves on its own.
Animate height yourself alongside it; the glide moves content with a compositor translate and never animates height.

usage.description: Returns a handle to pass to a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible. When that component changes size, it and the content after it inside `containerRef` animate together on one shared motion role. Fixed and stuck sticky elements stay put, the glide never scrolls the area, and Reduce Motion is respected. It applies under every pointer, a mouse included. Without the handle a component keeps its jump: content after it takes its place at once. Content after the change may mix Astryx components and your own elements; none of it opts in.

dense.description: Animates the element behind ref (x, y, scale, rotate, opacity) with Astryx's motion; returns the animator.

paramDescriptions.ref: The element ref; share it with a gesture hook to drag and animate one element.

returnDescriptions.animator: animate(target, {velocity?}), decay(velocity), set, get, getVelocity, stop; stable, never re-renders.

bestPractices.description: Pass the release velocity to animate after a drag.
Keep animated values in state; read animator.get().

usage.description: Spring with animate, fling with decay, follow a finger with set. Reduce Motion: a cross-fade on touch, at once with a mouse; decay keeps its momentum.

params.description: The ref of the one element to animate, the same ref you pass to the element: another hook, such as a gesture hook, can take it too, so a drag and an animation share one element. After every render the animator follows the element behind it. When the element unmounts its motion stops and its values return to rest, so a remount starts at rest, and so does a node that replaces it. Before the element mounts, and while it is unmounted, every call does nothing and `animate` and `decay` resolve at once.
params.name: ref

returns.description: The element's animator, the same object on every render: `animate(target, {velocity?})` springs channels to a target on the state-change motion Astryx's components use, `decay(velocity)` coasts them from a release velocity, `set(values)` jumps them, `get()` and `getVelocity()` read them, and `stop()` halts them. The channels are `x` and `y` (px), `scale` (1 at the element's size), `rotate` (degrees) and `opacity` (0 to 1). `animate` and `decay` return a promise that resolves when the motion ends. Calling it never re-renders the component. Calls before the ref attaches do nothing and resolve at once.
returns.name: animator

accessibility.description: An animator moves an element; it adds no way to act. Give every action an animation stands for a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as a button that discards a card, and have it call `animate`, which Reduce Motion turns into a fade in place. Keep `decay` for a throw the person made: Reduce Motion keeps the momentum of a coast, as it continues that throw. Keep focus on an element that stays on screen: move it before you fling its element away.
accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology

accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, every call is planned for them. On a touch screen a move or a scale becomes a short opacity cross-fade: the element fades out where it was and fades back in where it lands. With a mouse it lands at once. A decay of `x` and `y` keeps its momentum, as it continues the throw the person made; a decay of `scale`, `rotate` or `opacity` is planned like a move. No option turns this off.
accessibility.name: Reduce Motion

bestPractices.description: Call the animator from event handlers and effects: it lives outside render, so animating never re-renders the component.
Start every `animate` that follows a drag with the release velocity, so the element carries on as it was thrown.
Reach every state an animation shows without the animation too: a key, a button or a menu item that calls the same code.
Keep the animated values in React state: read them with `animator.get()` when you need them.

usage.description: Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use. Call `animator.animate` to spring an element to new values on the state-change motion, `animator.decay` to fling it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `animator.set` to move it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props. Outside React, use `createAnimator`.

dense.description: Imperative screen-reader announcements via a visually-hidden live region: the page-body one, or one inside the open Astryx modal the caller is rendered in (a native modal hides the body region). Polite + assertive regions created empty on first use + kept mounted, so announcements are reliable (most AT ignore a live region inserted together w/ its content). Messages auto-clear after ~2s.

paramDescriptions.options.hasReplace: instance states one current state (e.g. a search's result count): each message withdraws the instance's previous one not yet spoken, whatever politeness, spoken at its own; spoken messages stay; other instances + instances w/o hasReplace still join. Default false.

returnDescriptions.announce: speaks message through the live region the caller is heard from: page body, or inside the open Astryx modal (Dialog, modal BottomSheet/Drawer, Lightbox, MobileNav, CommandPalette) the calling component is rendered in. politeness defaults "polite"; same-frame messages join in order, identical repeat kept once, except a hasReplace instance replaces its own not-yet-spoken message; empty message clears lingering + not-yet-spoken status.

bestPractices.description: Use instead of hand-rolled aria-live div; region rendered w/ its content usually does not announce.
"polite" for status / counts; "assertive" only for errors + time-sensitive alerts (it interrupts).
Announce outcome, not interaction; "12 results", not "search ran".
Changing value (result count while typing): own useAnnounce({hasReplace: true}) instance, so faster-than-a-frame input says only the latest.
Announce content already visible + labeled in DOM; doubles up for AT users.

usage.description: Announces visual-only state to screen readers: result counts, "no results", loading / saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3). Regions mounted empty up front, so updates announce; text auto-clears so stale status does not linger in a11y tree.

params.description: Configuration object.
params.name: options

params.description: The instance states one current state, such as a search's result count: each message it writes withdraws the instance's previous message while that one has not been spoken yet, whatever their politeness, and is spoken at its own politeness. A message already spoken stays. Messages from other instances, and from instances without hasReplace, still join. Give each state a component reports its own instance, for example one for the result count and one for selection changes.
params.name: options.hasReplace

returns.description: Speaks a message through the live region the caller can be heard from: the shared one on the page body, or, when the calling component is rendered inside an open Astryx modal (Dialog, modal BottomSheet, modal Drawer, Lightbox, MobileNav, CommandPalette), a persistent region inside that modal, since a native modal hides the page-body region from assistive technology. Politeness defaults to "polite"; messages announced in the same frame are joined, in order, into one announcement, and an identical repeat is kept once, except that each message from a hasReplace instance replaces the previous message of that instance not yet spoken. An empty message clears any lingering status, including joined messages not yet spoken, instead of announcing.
returns.name: announce

bestPractices.description: Reach for this instead of hand-rolling an aria-live div; a region rendered with its content usually does not announce at all.
Keep "polite" for status and result counts; reserve "assertive" for errors and time-sensitive alerts, since it interrupts whatever the screen reader is saying.
Announce the outcome, not the interaction; "12 results" rather than "search ran".
Send a value that keeps changing, such as a result count as the user types, through its own useAnnounce({hasReplace: true}) instance, so input faster than a frame says only the latest count.
Announce content that is already visible and correctly labeled in the DOM; that doubles up for screen reader users.

usage.description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.

ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list or move the active option; Enter (and Space without search) picks it or opens the list; Escape and Tab close it; Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump to the first or last option. An editable control that keeps Home and End for the caret does not pass them to this handler, as CommandPalette does.
returns.name: onKeyDown

returns.description: Picks an option from a press on it, then closes the list.
returns.name: onItemSelect

returns.description: Makes the hovered option active without scrolling the list or moving focus.
returns.name: onItemMouseEnter

returns.description: Props for a single-line `input` you render: `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls` only while the listbox renders (`isOpen` with at least one option), `aria-activedescendant` only while an option is active, and the field’s key handler. Pass your own `onKeyDown` here rather than beside the spread: it runs after the hook’s handler unless that handler claimed the key, and it may be typed for its element.
returns.name: getFieldProps

returns.description: Props for the listbox you render, anywhere in the document, including the page’s flow: its `id` and `role`, and a press handler that keeps focus in the field. Render it while `isOpen` and there are options, and name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
returns.name: getListboxProps

returns.description: Props for the option at `index`: its `id`, `role`, `aria-selected` (true on the active option), `aria-disabled` on a disabled one, a pointer move that makes it active without moving focus, and a press that picks it.
returns.name: getOptionProps

accessibility.description: With the prop getters, moving the active option never moves focus out of the field. The field names the active option through `aria-activedescendant` and carries none while no option is active.
accessibility.name: Focus stays in the field

accessibility.description: While the listbox renders, the field exposes `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` naming it. Otherwise it exposes `aria-expanded="false"` and references nothing.
accessibility.name: Expanded state follows the list

accessibility.description: The field is a `combobox` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`. The list is a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected="true"` on the active one. You name the field and the listbox.
accessibility.name: Roles

accessibility.description: While the list shows, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the active option and wrap; Enter picks an active option and only then stops the field’s own Enter; Escape, whatever modifier is held, hides the list without closing an enclosing dialog or popover on the same press. While it is hidden, ArrowDown shows it when there are options. An open field with no options still takes Escape, which closes the list, so render an empty message while it is open. Home, End, other chords such as Shift+Enter, and every other key reach the field.
accessibility.name: Keys

accessibility.description: No key moves, picks or hides while an input method is composing text.
accessibility.name: Input method

accessibility.description: Moving the pointer over an option makes it active without moving focus; pressing an option picks it, and the field keeps focus through the press.
accessibility.name: Pointer

accessibility.description: Yours to announce: compose useAnnounce (AST-075 DEC-2) so each new query announces the number of options, or that there are none, once and politely. For none, announce the words the field shows.
accessibility.name: Result count

bestPractices.description: Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and set the control's `aria-activedescendant` only while `isOpen` and `highlightedIndex` points at a rendered option, as CommandPalette does.
For type-to-select without a search field, run useTypeahead's handler first and fall through to this `onKeyDown` when it returns false, as Selector does.
For a field you render, spread the prop getters, and set the active option yourself when a new query changes the options: the first option so Enter picks it, or -1 so Enter stays the field’s.
Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query (AST-075 DEC-2). When nothing matches, announce the words the field shows for it.
Render controls that are not options, such as a create button or an empty message, inside the listbox; render them beside it.
Move DOM focus onto the options; the active option is announced through `aria-activedescendant` while focus stays on the control.

usage.description: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.

dense.description: Headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it on hover / keyboard focus: the "row actions appear on hover" pattern. CSS-only: no hover state in React, no re-render on hover. Caller authors no StyleX; hook hands out container + content styles; a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus. Accessible: revealed content visually hidden at rest via position + opacity (never display:none), stays mounted + in tab order + announced; reveals on :focus-within, stays visible under a coarse primary pointer, honors prefers-reduced-motion.

paramDescriptions.options.isEnabled: when false hook is inert: no container styles, content getters return no styles, content always shown. Read every render, so it can flip after mount.

returnDescriptions.getContainerProps: spread onto container whose hover/focus-within drives reveal. Accepts hoverDelay (ms dwell before reveal starts: hover-intent gate like Tooltip / HoverCard delay) + forceState ("active" | "inactive") to pin trigger state when a caller owns it. "inactive" yields to keyboard focus + coarse pointers.
returnDescriptions.getContentRevealProps: spread onto each revealed / concealed child. Accepts isRevealInverted (conceal-on-hover), isLayoutPreserved (reserve layout box while hidden) + forceVisibility ("shown" | "hidden") to pin this element regardless of container. "hidden" yields to focus.

bestPractices.description: Destructure getContainerProps + getContentRevealProps; spread getContainerProps() on container (via mergeProps w/ your stylex.props) + getContentRevealProps() on content to reveal.
Use for secondary affordances: reveal-on-hover row actions (edit/copy/remove on list / table rows) + overlay controls on card / media tile (e.g. Thumbnail remove button).
Gate reveal w/ isEnabled when a consumer prop decides revealed-on-hover vs always shown; can change at any time.
Pass isLayoutPreserved for absolutely-positioned / overlay content to reserve its box + avoid layout shift.
Set hoverDelay (100-250ms) on rows in a long list so a travelling cursor does not light up every row; keyboard + touch still reveal immediately.
forceState when something else owns the interaction (drag, scroll / motion gate, open row menu); forceVisibility when one element should ignore the container.
Reach past the API into private custom properties (--_reveal-opacity etc) to suppress a reveal; use forceState / forceVisibility.
Use to hide content that must always be discoverable; keep essential actions visible instead of gating behind hover.

usage.description: Headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it on hover / keyboard focus: the "row actions appear on hover" pattern. CSS-only: no hover state in React, no re-render on hover. Caller authors no StyleX; hook hands out container + content styles; a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus. Accessible: revealed content visually hidden at rest via position + opacity (never display:none), stays mounted + in tab order + announced; reveals on :focus-within, stays visible under a coarse primary pointer, honors prefers-reduced-motion.

params.description: Configuration object for the reveal container. Optional.
params.name: options

params.description: When false the hook is inert: the container gets no styles and content getters return no styles, so content is always shown. Read on every render, so a component can flip it after mount (e.g. revealOn === "hover").
params.name: options.isEnabled

returns.description: Spread onto the container whose hover/focus-within drives the reveal. Accepts hoverDelay (ms the pointer must dwell before the reveal starts: a hover-intent gate like Tooltip's and HoverCard's delay, so a cursor sweeping across a list leaves nothing painted behind it) and forceState ("active" | "inactive") to pin the trigger state when a caller owns it: a motion gate, a scroll, or a row whose menu is open. "inactive" still yields to keyboard focus and coarse pointers.
returns.name: getContainerProps

returns.description: Spread onto each revealed / concealed child. Accepts isRevealInverted to conceal-on-hover instead of reveal-on-hover, isLayoutPreserved to reserve the layout box while hidden (opacity-only) and avoid layout shift, and forceVisibility ("shown" | "hidden") to pin this one element's appearance whatever the container is doing. "hidden" yields to focus.
returns.name: getContentRevealProps

bestPractices.description: Destructure getContainerProps and getContentRevealProps; spread getContainerProps() on the container (via mergeProps with your own stylex.props) and getContentRevealProps() on the content to reveal.
Use for secondary affordances: reveal-on-hover row actions (edit/copy/remove on list or table rows) and overlay controls on a card or media tile (e.g. Thumbnail's remove button).
Gate the reveal with isEnabled when a consumer prop decides whether content is revealed on hover or always shown; it can change at any time.
Pass isLayoutPreserved for absolutely-positioned or overlay content to reserve its box and avoid layout shift when it appears.
Set a hoverDelay (100-250ms) on rows in a long list, so a cursor travelling across the list does not light up every row it passes; keyboard and touch still reveal immediately.

Reach for forceState when something other than the pointer owns the interaction (a drag, a scroll or motion gate, an open row menu), and forceVisibility when just one element should ignore the container.
Reach past the API into the hook's private custom properties (--_reveal-opacity and friends) to suppress a reveal; use forceState / forceVisibility, which survive a rename.
Use it to hide content that must always be discoverable; keep essential actions visible instead of gating them behind hover.

usage.description: A headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it when the container is hovered or receives keyboard focus: the classic "row actions appear on hover" pattern. The reveal is CSS-only: no hover state lives in React and hovering never triggers a re-render. The caller authors no StyleX for the reveal itself; the hook hands out the container and content styles, and a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus into one another. Accessible by construction: revealed content is visually hidden at rest with position and opacity (never display:none), so it stays mounted, keeps its place in the tab order, and is announced to assistive technology; it reveals on :focus-within so keyboard users see it when tabbing in, stays visible under a coarse primary pointer (never gated behind hover there), and honors prefers-reduced-motion.

dense.description: Dev-only "Component: message" console warning, once per mount while condition holds. Ref + effect, so it never repeats per render nor causes a re-render. Outside a component, use the imperative devWarn utility.

paramDescriptions.component: component / hook name, used as message prefix.
paramDescriptions.message: what went wrong + how to fix it.

bestPractices.description: Say what is wrong + what to do instead; the message is the value.
Warn about combinations types cannot express (mutually exclusive props set together).
Use for user-visible problems / runtime error handling; it is dev-only.

usage.description: Render-safe guardrail warning from inside a component. Stripped from production builds.

params.name: message

params.description: Whether to warn.
params.name: condition

bestPractices.description: Say what is wrong and what the builder should do instead; the message is the whole value of the warning.
Warn about combinations the types cannot express, such as two mutually exclusive props being set together.
Use it for anything a user could see or for runtime error handling; it is stripped from production builds.

usage.description: Fires a dev-only "Component: message" console warning once per mount while the condition holds. It is the render-safe way for a component to flag misuse: warning straight from the render body repeats on every render, and gating it with state adds a re-render, so this uses a ref and an effect instead. For a warning outside a component, use the imperative devWarn utility.

dense.description: Returns the current text direction ('ltr' or 'rtl') during render. Render-time last resort: prefer CSS logical properties first.

returnDescriptions.direction: ambient text direction ('ltr' or 'rtl'), defaulting to 'ltr'.

bestPractices.description: Prefer CSS logical properties before using useDirection.
Use for HTML canvas rendering where time/value axes start from the logical inline start edge.
Use to conditionally swap styles that CSS logical properties solve directly.

usage.description: Reads ambient text direction during render. Prefer CSS logical properties, icon mirror styles, and DOM reads first. Use for canvas drawing or non-CSS coordinate calculation.

returns.description: The ambient text direction ('ltr' or 'rtl') from the enclosing InternationalizationProvider, falling back to 'ltr' when called outside a provider.

bestPractices.description: Prefer CSS logical properties and directional CSS mirroring before using useDirection.
Use useDirection when drawing on an HTML canvas or calculating non-CSS layout coordinates where the start edge depends on text direction.
Use useDirection to conditionally swap margins, paddings, or inline alignments that can be solved with CSS logical properties.

usage.description: Reads the current text direction during render. Reach for this hook as a last resort when render-time direction is strictly required (such as canvas drawing that cannot use CSS logical properties). In order of preference, always favor: CSS logical properties (margin-inline, inset-inline); shared mirror styles for directional icons (CSS scaleX); and DOM reads for keyboard or gesture logic.

dense.description: A drag that settles the element at ref on snap points (px offsets): {settleTo}.

paramDescriptions.options.flickThreshold: px/s past which a release carries one snap point; 1008.
paramDescriptions.options.onSettle: (index) once settled; latest one is called.
paramDescriptions.options.snapPoints: Ascending px offsets from the resting position.

bestPractices.description: Wire settleTo to buttons and keys.
Rebuild a sheet or carousel with it.

usage.description: Nearest snap point, the next on a flick, the start when moving back; the settle keeps the release velocity. Sheets and carousels: use their props.

params.description: A ref to the element a drag moves, along `axis` only.
params.name: ref

params.description: The axis the element moves along. A new one creates the drag again, starting where the element is.
params.name: options.axis

params.description: Offsets in px along `axis` from the element's resting position, such as `[0, 240, 480]`, sorted before use (`onSettle` and `settleTo` count in that order); an empty list makes the drag do nothing. Unlike BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, they are not fractions of the viewport. New ones create the drag again and nothing more: the element stays where it is, a settle in flight included, and the next drag or `settleTo` starts there.
params.name: options.snapPoints

params.description: A release faster than this, in px/s, carries to the next snap point in its direction. The default is the flick speed measured for UIKit's sheet. A new one creates the drag again, as new snap points do.
params.name: options.flickThreshold

params.description: Called with the snap point's index once the element settles on it. The latest function is the one called, so it may be new on every render.
params.name: options.onSettle

returns.description: Settles the element on the snap point at `index` without a drag: the keyboard path. The same function on every render.
returns.name: settleTo

accessibility.description: A drag is one way in, never the only one. Give each snap point a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as Expand and Collapse buttons, and call `settleTo` from it. When a position changes what the element shows, announce the change.
accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology

accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the settle after a touch drag becomes a short cross-fade into the snap point, as does any settle on a device whose primary pointer is coarse, such as a tablet; after a mouse or pen drag elsewhere it lands at once. `settleTo` fades on such a device and lands at once with a fine primary pointer. While the finger is down, the element still follows it.
accessibility.name: Reduce Motion

bestPractices.description: Offer the same positions without a drag: buttons or keys that call `settleTo`.
Keep the settled index in state from `onSettle`, and render what the position means from it.
Use it for a sheet or a carousel: their own props already settle the way people expect.

usage.description: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Outside React, use `createDragToSnapPoints`.

dense.description: Returns StyleX style for animating element on mount. Only animates when element dynamically inserted after initial page paint; elements rendered on page load not animated. returnDescriptions.entryStyle: StyleX style object for entry animation / null if element rendered on initial page load (no animation needed).

Spread returned style into stylex.props() alongside other styles.
Use for elements that should be visible on initial page load; they will not animate.

Uses Astryx motion tokens (duration, easing) for consistent timing. Server-rendered elements hydrate without entry style, never animate; elements mounted after hydration animate.

dense.description: Traps focus within container element following WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to document focus events + redirects focus back into container if a Tab from inside moves focus out. Handles both Tab + Shift+Tab wrapping. Tab pressed while focus outside container left to the page. Mouse clicks outside container not intercepted; use light-dismiss handler for that.

paramDescriptions.options.onEscape: callback when Escape key pressed inside trapped container.

returnDescriptions.focusFirst: focuses first focusable element inside container.

Use on non-modal content like tooltips / dropdowns; those need light-dismiss, not focus trapping.

usage.description: Traps focus within container element following WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to document focus events + redirects focus back into container if a Tab from inside moves focus out. Handles both Tab + Shift+Tab wrapping. Tab pressed while focus outside container left to the page. On deactivate/unmount, restores focus to the element focused before activation unless focus already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap. Mouse clicks outside container not intercepted; use light-dismiss handler for that.

usage.description: Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.

dense.description: Manages keyboard navigation within 2D grid following WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Supports arrow keys for cell-to-cell navigation, Home/End for row boundaries, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End for grid boundaries, Page Up/Down for custom callbacks (e.g. month navigation in calendars). Boundary navigation callbacks allow cross-grid navigation.

paramDescriptions.options.cellSelector: selector for grid cells in DOM order (incl. disabled/empty) so geometry is preserved.
paramDescriptions.options.columns: # columns in grid. Used for up/down navigation (moves by this many cells).
paramDescriptions.options.getFocusTarget: resolve element to focus for a cell (e.g. button inside gridcell wrapper). Omit = focus the cell.
paramDescriptions.options.hasRovingTabIndex: own a single roving tab stop across the grid (one focus target tabindex=0, rest -1); repaired on render + moved with arrows. Attach handleFocus to onFocus. default false.
paramDescriptions.options.isCellFocusable: predicate for whether a matched cell can take focus. Omit = all focusable.
paramDescriptions.options.onNavigateAfter: callback when navigation would go after last cell. Receives column index + offset.
paramDescriptions.options.onNavigateBefore: callback when navigation would go before first cell. Receives column index + offset (1 for horizontal, columns for vertical).
paramDescriptions.options.onPageDown: callback for Page Down key (e.g. next month in calendars); receives the key event (shiftKey → e.g. a year).
paramDescriptions.options.onPageUp: callback for Page Up key (e.g. previous month in calendars); receives the key event (shiftKey → e.g. a year).

returnDescriptions.focusLast: focus last focusable cell in grid.

dense.description: Global keyboard shortcuts w/ one window keydown listener per hook instance. Handlers kept in ref; re-renders never re-subscribe. Skips typing targets (input/textarea/select/contenteditable) unless allowInInputs, skips defaultPrevented and IME key events (even with allowInInputs), preventDefault() on match. "mod" = ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere. SSR-safe.

paramDescriptions.hotkeys: array of { keys, onPress, allowInInputs?, isDisabled? }. keys = "+"-separated combo ("mod+k", "?", "escape"). Shifted punctuation = produced char ("?", not "shift+/"); final key compared vs event.key; on Apple platforms (macOS; iPadOS/iOS with a hardware keyboard) an alt combo (letter/digit/punctuation/space) also matches the US key position (event.code) when Option typed a dead key or non-ASCII char, else the typed char; there shifted punctuation as alt+shift+/.

bestPractices.description: Use for app-level shortcuts: command palettes (mod+k), help overlays ("?"), navigation keys.
Pair w/ Kbd component to display same combo registered; both resolve "mod" per platform identically.
Use isDisabled to suspend shortcuts while modal/wizard owns keyboard, instead of unmounting hook.
Use for focus-scoped keyboard nav inside widget; use useListFocus / useGridFocus instead.

usage.description: Global keyboard shortcuts w/ one window keydown listener per hook instance. Handlers kept in ref; re-renders never re-subscribe. Skips typing targets unless allowInInputs, skips defaultPrevented and IME key events (even with allowInInputs), preventDefault() on match. SSR-safe.

params.description: Shortcut registrations. Each entry: `{ keys, onPress, allowInInputs?, isDisabled? }`. `keys` is a "+"-separated combo like "mod+k", "?", "escape"; "mod" is ⌘ on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Register a punctuation key that shift changes as the character it produces: "?", not "shift+/", because the final key is compared against `event.key`. On Apple platforms (macOS, and iPadOS or iOS with a hardware keyboard), where Option changes the typed character (Option+A types "å"), an "alt" combo with a letter, digit, punctuation or space key also matches that key at its US position, on every layout, when Option typed a dead key or a non-ASCII character; when Option types a plain ASCII character, the combo matches that character (a German Mac types "@" for Option+L, so it fires "alt+@"). On Apple platforms, name shifted punctuation as "alt+shift+/", not "alt+?". `onPress` receives the KeyboardEvent after preventDefault(). `allowInInputs` (default false) lets the hotkey fire while typing in inputs/textareas/selects/contenteditable. `isDisabled` temporarily disables the entry.

Both modes use theme body defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged; establish intentional groups and complete required providers inside the rendered layer.

Placement/alignment logical: mapped to logical anchor() insets resolved against the popover's inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS). `positioning: "custom"` (context mode) = author position styles yourself via `style`; keeps popover behavior + position-anchor wiring, derives nothing (incl. RTL mirroring, which becomes yours). `offset` (context mode) = clearance from the anchor as a CSS length (number = px), applied to both edges of the placement axis so it survives a flip; layers are flush by default. Context mode begins with an inert `<template>` marker for stable SSR/hydration, then keeps the final layer inline at a safe JSX position or portals it to the nearest safe ancestor; CSS custom properties keep inheriting from that host while direction and writing mode are preserved from the JSX position. `lazyMount` waits for show and unmounts content on hide while the marker remains. The Popover API top layer escapes clipping/stacking wherever it is hosted. Viewport overflow: flips to opposite side, then slides along the alignment axis; stays on screen even when the trigger runs past the edge, as long as it fits between the gutters.

returns.description: Render function for the popover element. Pass placement/alignment in context mode or x/y in fixed mode. Placement/alignment are logical: they map to logical anchor() insets, which resolve against the popover's own inherited direction, so RTL contexts mirror automatically in pure CSS. Pass `positioning: "custom"` in context mode to author position styles yourself via `style` (e.g. explicit anchor() insets or an anchor-size() cover): the hook keeps the popover behavior and position-anchor wiring but derives no position styles, including the automatic RTL mirroring, which becomes your responsibility. Pass `offset` (a CSS length; a number is px) in context mode for clearance from the anchor: it applies to both edges of the placement axis, so the gap survives a flip. Layers are flush by default. Context mode first renders an inert `<template>` marker in matching server and client markup. The final layer stays at that JSX position if its parent is safe; otherwise it is portaled to the nearest ancestor outside paragraphs, links, buttons, inline formatting, and structurally restricted containers. The nearest safe host keeps CSS custom properties inheriting live, while the layer preserves direction and writing mode from its JSX position. By default this resolution occurs after hydration so closed-layer DOM remains available, and it re-renders only the slot that holds the marker and the layer, not the component that called the hook (which renders again only when a resolved mount is replaced by a render call that moved to another host); `lazyMount` defers it until `show()` and unmounts the content again on hide while the marker remains. The Popover API promotes the layer to the top layer when shown, so it escapes ancestor clipping and stacking wherever it is hosted. When the layer would overflow the viewport, position-try fallbacks flip it to the opposite side, then slide it along the alignment axis, so it stays on screen near viewport edges, even when its trigger runs past the edge, as long as the layer fits between the viewport gutters.
returns.name: render

bestPractices.description: Use context mode for anchor-positioned overlays relative to a trigger element, and fixed mode for manually positioned overlays at specific coordinates.
Build on higher-level components like Popover, HoverCard, and Tooltip for common overlay patterns.

Rely on the Popover API top layer to escape ancestor clipping and stacking, and host the layer near its trigger rather than in the body so it inherits the trigger's theme cascade and keeps a natural focus order. Without the Popover API there is no top layer, and content with a higher `z-index` can cover the layer. In context mode a layer with no position of its own stays in the page flow, so an ancestor that clips overflow can clip it. In fixed mode a transformed ancestor is its containing block, so that ancestor can move and clip it.
Implement ARIA patterns directly in a Layer unless you also own the full accessibility behavior.

Apply intentional formatting through render styles or content, and establish complete content-local providers inside the rendered layer.

usage.description: Use when one element needs a forwarded consumer ref plus internal refs. Keeps the callback stable across unrelated rerenders.

params.description: Up to six refs that should all receive the same element.
params.name: refs

returns.description: A merged callback ref that remains stable until an input ref changes.
returns.name: ref

bestPractices.description: Use useMergedRefs when one element must receive both a forwarded ref and one or more internal refs.
Call mergeRefs directly in a JSX ref prop; that creates a new callback on every render and forces unnecessary detach and attach work.

usage.description: Combines multiple object or callback refs into one stable callback ref. Use it when a component must forward a consumer ref while also attaching internal refs. Unlike calling mergeRefs during render, the callback identity stays stable across unrelated rerenders, so React does not detach and reattach the element.

dense.description: Multi-select combobox state + keys; focus stays on control. Powers MultiSelector. Toggle keeps list open; rows may carry an action cell (grid). Renders nothing, sets no attrs: caller renders + wires ARIA.

paramDescriptions.options.hasSearch: own search field: Space types, press / Enter opening does not pre-highlight (ArrowDown/Up still first / last enabled), Delete / Backspace edit query, no type-to-select. Home / End still jump; stop them first to keep them for the caret, use PageUp / PageDown.
paramDescriptions.options.hasValue: anything selected; clear skipped when false.
paramDescriptions.options.isGrid: rows = option + action cell; inline-end / inline-start arrows move between them (RTL-aware); Enter on action -> onActivateAction.
paramDescriptions.options.listboxId: listbox / grid id; option + action-cell ids derive from it.
paramDescriptions.options.onActivateAction: grid: run highlighted row's action; selection unchanged.
paramDescriptions.options.onClear: clear all; Delete / Backspace on closed control. ignored when open or hasSearch.
paramDescriptions.options.onOpen: show list; return false to refuse (highlight untouched).
paramDescriptions.options.onToggle: add / remove value; list stays open.
paramDescriptions.options.rowHasAction: grid: row at index has an action cell.
paramDescriptions.options.selectableItems: options in render order; disabled ones not toggleable, skipped while moving in open list; opening lands on the first / last enabled option (ArrowUp: last).

returnDescriptions.activeDescendantId: control aria-activedescendant: active option or its action cell; undefined when closed / none.
returnDescriptions.getActionCellId: grid: id for action cell of row index.
returnDescriptions.onItemMouseEnter: hover makes option / action cell active; no scroll, no focus move.
returnDescriptions.onKeyDown: control keydown: ArrowDown/Up open or move; Enter (Space w/o search) toggles, stays open; Escape / Tab close; Home / End / PageUp / PageDown jump; typed chars jump to the next option by label prefix, as in Selector (w/o search); Space still toggles.
returnDescriptions.onTriggerClick: toggle list from a press on control.
returnDescriptions.setHighlightedIndex: set active row (lands on option cell).

bestPractices.description: Option id = getItemId(index); control aria-activedescendant = activeDescendantId.
isGrid only when rows carry a control; action cell id = getActionCellId(index).
Announce result count via useAnnounce on new query.
Close after each toggle; multi-select stays open.

usage.description: Headless multi-select combobox: active option + keys, focus stays on control; toggle keeps list open. Caller renders + wires ARIA.

params.description: Configuration object.
params.name: options

params.description: The options in the same order as they render. Options with `disabled` cannot be toggled and are skipped while moving through the open list. Opening never lands on a disabled option: ArrowUp opens on the last enabled option, and ArrowDown, a press, Enter or Space on the first enabled option.
params.name: options.selectableItems

params.description: Whether the list is shown. The caller owns this state.
params.name: options.isOpen

params.description: Called to show the list. Return `false` to refuse; the hook then leaves the highlight alone.
params.name: options.onOpen

params.description: Called to hide the list. The highlight resets first.
params.name: options.onClose

params.description: Called with the value of the option to add or remove. Toggling keeps the list open.
params.name: options.onToggle

params.description: The listbox (or grid) element's id. Option and action-cell ids are derived from it.
params.name: options.listboxId

params.description: Whether the list has its own search field. Space then types instead of toggling, opening by a press or Enter does not pre-highlight (ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the first and last enabled option), Delete and Backspace edit the query, and type-to-select is off. Home and End still jump to the first and last option, so a search input that keeps them for the caret should stop them before this handler and rely on PageUp and PageDown.
params.name: options.hasSearch

params.description: Clears every selected value. When provided, Delete or Backspace on the closed control clears them, so clearing is not pointer-only. Ignored while the list is open or with `hasSearch`.
params.name: options.onClear

params.description: Whether anything is selected. The Delete and Backspace clear is skipped when false.
params.name: options.hasValue

params.description: Whether each row pairs an option cell with an action cell. The inline-end arrow then moves the highlight to the row's action and the inline-start arrow back, following visual direction in right-to-left layouts, and Enter on the action runs `onActivateAction` instead of toggling.
params.name: options.isGrid

params.description: In a grid, whether the row at `index` has an action cell to move to.
params.name: options.rowHasAction

params.description: In a grid, runs the control in the highlighted row's action cell. The selection does not change.
params.name: options.onActivateAction

params.description: Whether the control ignores clicks and keys.
params.name: options.isDisabled

returns.description: Index of the active row, or -1 when none is active.
returns.name: highlightedIndex

returns.description: Sets the active row, for example after filtering. The highlight lands on the row's option cell.
returns.name: setHighlightedIndex

returns.description: Which cell of the active row is highlighted; `'action'` only in a grid.
returns.name: highlightedCell

returns.description: The id to pass as the control's `aria-activedescendant`: the active option, or its action cell in a grid. Undefined while the list is closed or nothing is active.
returns.name: activeDescendantId

returns.description: The id to render on the option at `index`.
returns.name: getItemId

returns.description: In a grid, the id to render on the action cell of row `index`.
returns.name: getActionCellId

returns.description: Toggles the list from a press on the control.
returns.name: onTriggerClick

returns.description: Key handler for the control that keeps focus. ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list or move the active row; Enter (and Space without search) toggles the active option and keeps the list open; Escape and Tab close it; Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump to the first or last option; without search, typed characters move to the next option whose label starts with them, as in Selector (a repeated letter cycles, and a single letter searches from the option after the active one), and Space still toggles.
returns.name: onKeyDown

returns.description: Makes the hovered option, or its action cell, active without scrolling the list or moving focus.
returns.name: onItemMouseEnter

bestPractices.description: Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and pass `activeDescendantId` as the control's `aria-activedescendant`.
Use `isGrid` only when rows carry a control next to the option; give each action cell `id={getActionCellId(index)}`.
Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query.
Close the list after each toggle; a multi-select stays open so several options can be picked in a row.

usage.description: Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.

dense.description: Outline items from h1-h6 inside a DOM element. Updates when those headings change. Empty when the ref is null.

returnDescriptions.items: one item per heading with an id and text, in order: id, trimmed label, level 1-6.

bestPractices.description: Give each listed heading an id. A heading without one is omitted.
Point the ref at the article, not the whole page.
Expect the hook to invent heading ids.
Use it for a Markdown string. useOutlineFromMarkdown matches Markdown.

usage.description: Outline items from headings already in the page. Pass them to Outline. A heading needs an id and text.

params.description: The element that holds the headings. The hook reads h1 through h6 inside it.
params.name: containerRef

returns.description: One item per heading that has both an id and text, in document order, ready for Outline's items prop. id is the heading's id, label is its trimmed text, and level is its depth from 1 to 6.
returns.name: items

bestPractices.description: Put an id on every heading the outline should list. A heading with no id, or with no text, is omitted.
Point the ref at the article, not the page, so headings outside the article stay out of the outline.
Expect the hook to invent ids. It only reads the ids the headings already have.
Use it for a Markdown string. useOutlineFromMarkdown follows the same parser and slugs as Markdown.

usage.description: Builds outline items from the headings already in the page. Use it when the article is not a Markdown string, and pass the items to Outline. The list updates when headings are added, removed, renamed, or given a new id. A null ref returns an empty list.

dense.description: Headings of a Markdown string as OutlineItem[] for an Outline beside the rendered document. Same parser and heading slugs as Markdown; memoized on source and options.

paramDescriptions.markdown: Markdown source; the same string you render with Markdown.
paramDescriptions.options: parse options; omit for a document without plugins.
paramDescriptions.options.isFinal: whether the source is complete; false while Markdown's isStreaming is true.
paramDescriptions.options.plugins: ordered plugin list; pass the same list to Markdown. New reference recomputes.

returnDescriptions.items: one item per root heading in document order: id is the rendered id in a complete document without sources, label is its text, level is 1-6.

bestPractices.description: Pass the same string, plugin list and finality to Markdown and the hook; items match the headings once content is complete.
Keep the plugin list stable; a new array each render recomputes.
Several documents on one page: one createMarkdownHeadingLinks per document with headingIdPrefix.
Write items by hand or find headings with a regex.
Expect every item to have a target while content streams; a heading can be absent or have another id until complete.
Expect an item to link to a heading that cites a Markdown sources entry; the hook does not receive sources, so the ids differ.
Expect items for nested headings; only root headings count.

usage.description: Headings of a Markdown string for an Outline next to the rendered document. Same parser and slugs as Markdown, so items link to their headings in a complete document. Outside React, use parseOutlineFromMarkdown.

params.description: The Markdown source. Pass the same string you render with Markdown.
params.name: markdown

params.description: Parse options. Omit them for a document that Markdown renders without plugins.
params.name: options

params.description: The ordered Markdown plugin list. Pass the same list to Markdown, so transforms, labels and ids agree. The outline is recomputed when the list reference changes.
params.name: options.plugins

params.description: Whether the source is complete. Pass false while Markdown's isStreaming is true, so both apply the same transforms.
params.name: options.isFinal

returns.description: One item per root heading, in document order, ready for Outline's items prop. id is the id Markdown renders on the heading in a complete document without sources, label is the heading's text, and level is its depth from 1 to 6.
returns.name: items

bestPractices.description: Pass the same string, plugin list and finality to Markdown and this hook, so items match the rendered headings once the content is complete.
Declare the plugin list outside the component or memoize it. A new array on each render recomputes the outline.
For several documents on one page, install one createMarkdownHeadingLinks per document with headingIdPrefix, so their ids do not collide.
Write the items by hand or find headings with a regular expression. They drift from the rendered ids.
Expect every item to have a target while content streams. Markdown reveals text gradually and trims unfinished syntax, so a heading can be absent or have another id until the content is complete.

Expect an item to link to a heading that cites a Markdown sources entry. The hook does not receive sources, so the ids differ: for '# Intro [ref]', Markdown renders intro and the hook returns intro-ref.
Expect an item for a nested heading, such as one in a blockquote. Only root headings become items.

usage.description: Extracts the headings of a Markdown string for an Outline next to the rendered document. It uses the parser and heading slugs that Markdown uses, so in a complete document each item links to its heading, and fenced code never counts as a heading. The result is memoized on the source and the options. Outside React, use parseOutlineFromMarkdown.

dense.description: Measures children rendered in hidden container to determine how many fit in available width w/o flickering. Uses ResizeObserver to react to container and measured-child size changes. Measurement container should hold all items plus optional overflow indicator element (identified by data-overflow-indicator attribute).

paramDescriptions.itemCount: total # items to measure for overflow.
paramDescriptions.options.behavior: which element to observe for overflow calculations. 'observeParent' uses container's parent element width, allowing visible container to remain content-sized.
paramDescriptions.options.collapseFrom: which end to collapse items from.
paramDescriptions.options.gap: gap between items in px. Used in width calculations.
paramDescriptions.options.minVisibleItems: min # items to always show, even if they don't fit.

returnDescriptions.containerRef: ref callback for visible container element.
returnDescriptions.measureRef: ref callback for hidden measurement container holding all items.
returnDescriptions.visibleCount: # items that fit in visible container.

bestPractices.description: Render all items into measureRef container (hidden) + only first visibleCount items into containerRef container (visible).
Include overflow indicator (e.g. "+N more" button) as last child of measurement container w/ data-overflow-indicator attribute.
Use for vertical overflow; this hook measures horizontal width only.

usage.description: Measures children rendered in hidden container to determine how many fit in available width w/o flickering. Uses ResizeObserver to react to container and measured-child size changes. Measurement container should hold all items plus optional overflow indicator element (identified by data-overflow-indicator attribute).

params.description: Total number of items to measure for overflow.
params.name: itemCount

params.description: Configuration object for overflow behavior.
params.name: options

params.description: Gap between items in pixels. Used in width calculations.
params.name: options.gap

params.description: Minimum number of items to always show, even if they don't fit.
params.name: options.minVisibleItems

params.description: which end to collapse items from.
params.name: options.collapseFrom

params.description: Which element to observe for overflow calculations. 'observeParent' uses the container's parent element width, allowing the visible container to remain content-sized.
params.name: options.behavior

returns.description: Ref callback to attach to the visible container element.
returns.name: containerRef

returns.description: Ref callback to attach to the hidden measurement container that holds all items.
returns.name: measureRef

returns.description: Number of items that fit in the visible container.
returns.name: visibleCount

returns.description: Whether any items are overflowing (visibleCount < itemCount).
returns.name: hasOverflow

bestPractices.description: Render all items into the measureRef container (hidden) and only the first visibleCount items into the containerRef container (visible).
Include an overflow indicator (e.g., "+N more" button) as the last child of the measurement container with a data-overflow-indicator attribute.
Use for vertical overflow; this hook measures horizontal width only.

usage.description: Measures children rendered in a hidden container to determine how many fit in the available width without flickering. Uses ResizeObserver to react to container and measured-child size changes. The measurement container should hold all items plus an optional overflow indicator element (identified by a data-overflow-indicator attribute).

dense.description: Overlay behavior on a container you already render (Card, media frame) w/o Overlay's wrapper. Spread containerRef + containerProps on it, render element / renderOverlay(children) once inside. CSS-driven via container :hover/:focus-within; hover mode also reveals on keyboard focus. With a mouse or trackpad, hidden content stays tabbable; focus reveals it. Keep other controls outside the area a revealed scrim covers (the scrim takes pointer input).

paramDescriptions.options.content: content inside the scrim; returned pre-rendered as element.
paramDescriptions.options.isOpen: controlled visibility; wins over showOn + touch toggle.
paramDescriptions.options.showOn: CSS visibility trigger. 'hover' also reveals on focus-within; 'hover-or-focus' = alias. Touch (hover: none): hover overlays toggle on tap.

returnDescriptions.containerProps: spread on the container: overlay scope className/style (positioned, clipped) + tap toggle handlers for hover overlays on touch devices.
returnDescriptions.element: scrim with content, render once inside the container; null w/o content.
returnDescriptions.renderOverlay: (children) => scrim; for dynamic content or self-mounted scrim. Use it or element.

bestPractices.description: showOn 'hover' for media card actions; also reveals on keyboard focus.
Label overlay actions by what they do; with a mouse or trackpad, Tab reaches them while hidden, focus reveals.
Use Overlay when there is no container to attach to.
Put info needed to choose the item (title, price) only in a hover/focus overlay; touch shows hover after a tap, never focus.

usage.description: Overlay behavior on an existing container: spread containerRef + containerProps, render element once inside. Scrim covers nearest positioned ancestor. CSS :hover/:focus-within; hover mode reveals on keyboard focus too; with a mouse or trackpad, hidden content stays tabbable.

params.description: Overlay configuration. Every field is optional.
params.name: options

params.description: Content to render inside the scrim. When set, the hook returns it pre-rendered as element.
params.name: options.content

params.description: Visibility trigger, read with CSS from the container. 'hover' also reveals on focus within the container for keyboard users; 'hover-or-focus' is an alias for it. On a touch device (hover: none), a hover overlay toggles on a tap on the container instead.
params.name: options.showOn

params.description: Controlled visibility. When set, it takes precedence over showOn and the touch toggle.
params.name: options.isOpen

params.description: Scrim background. false renders the content with no scrim background.
params.name: options.scrim

params.description: Where the scrim sits: over the whole positioned area, or as a strip along its bottom or top edge.
params.name: options.position

params.description: Alignment of the content within the scrim.
params.name: options.align

returns.description: Attach to the container element.
returns.name: containerRef

returns.description: Spread on the same container: className and style mark it as the overlay scope (positioned, clipped), and on a touch device with a hover overlay onClick and onMouseUp toggle it on a tap.
returns.name: containerProps

returns.description: The scrim with options.content, ready to render once inside the container. null when content is not set.
returns.name: element

returns.description: Renders the scrim around the children you pass, for content that changes or a scrim you mount yourself. Use it or element, not both.
returns.name: renderOverlay

bestPractices.description: Use showOn 'hover' for actions on media cards: it also reveals on keyboard focus within the container.
Give an overlay action a label that names what it does. With a mouse or trackpad, Tab reaches it while the overlay is hidden, and focus reveals the overlay.
Use the Overlay component when you do not already have a container element to attach to.

Put information people need to choose the item, such as its title or price, only in a hover or focus overlay; on a touch device a hover overlay shows only after a tap, and a focus overlay does not show.

usage.description: Adds overlay behavior to a container you already render, such as a Card or a custom media frame, without the wrapper Overlay adds. Spread containerRef and containerProps on the container, then render element (or renderOverlay(children)) once inside it. The scrim is absolutely positioned, so it covers the nearest positioned ancestor: the container itself, or a positioned section inside it such as an image area. Visibility is CSS-driven from the container's :hover and :focus-within, so with showOn 'hover' a keyboard user reveals the content by moving focus into the container. On a device with a mouse or trackpad, content that a hover or focus reveal hides stays in the tab order, so Tab reaches an action in it and focus reveals the scrim. On a touch-primary device a hover overlay stays inert until a tap. A revealed scrim takes pointer input over the area it covers, so keep any other control in the container outside the scrim, or use a top or bottom strip and keep the control in the part the strip leaves uncovered.

dense.description: Reports a drag as values ({state, translation, velocity}) for a surface you move yourself; a finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it, though a mouse or pen drag on selectable text selects it instead (give that text user-select: none). Claims at UIKit’s 10 pt; taps, presses and long presses are never a pan, and with axis a scroll across it stays the page’s. Thin layer over createPanGesture(element, options) → {destroy}. No keyboard path of its own: give the drag another way (WCAG 2.5.7). Reduce Motion: honor it in the animation you drive. Prefer BottomSheet snapPoints / Carousel hasSnap when they fit.

paramDescriptions.options.axis: 'x' | 'y': limit to one axis; the other is never reported and reads 0.
paramDescriptions.options.onPan: ({state, translation, velocity}): state 'began' | 'changed' | 'ended' | 'cancelled'; translation px since the drag began (threshold travel excluded, no jump); velocity px/s, release velocity at 'ended', 0 at 'cancelled'. Read through a ref.
paramDescriptions.ref: element to drag; one pan per node, re-created when the ref moves, destroyed at unmount.

returnDescriptions.void: nothing (no recognizer). createPanGesture returns {destroy}: removes every listener, cancels a drag in progress.

bestPractices.description: Move from translation + the offset at began, so the element moves with the finger from the claim.
Hand the ended velocity to the settling animation.
Give every drag a keyboard and assistive-technology alternative.
Use a component's own prop when it covers the job.
Hold the drag offset in a large component’s state.
Recognize taps or long presses with it.

usage.description: Drag as values for a card, a drawer handle, any surface you move. Thin layer over createPanGesture. No keyboard path of its own (WCAG 2.5.7); Reduce Motion applies to what you animate. Prefer component props (BottomSheet snapPoints, Carousel hasSnap).

params.description: The element to drag. The hook creates one pan for the element behind the ref, creates a new one when the ref moves to another node or `axis` changes, and destroys it at unmount; a drag in progress then ends without a `cancelled` event, since an effect never calls `onPan`.
params.name: ref

params.description: Configuration object.
params.name: options

params.description: Limits the drag to one axis. A drag along the other axis is not reported, and that component of every value reads 0. Omit it to report both axes.
params.name: options.axis

params.description: Called with `{state, translation, velocity}` as the drag begins, changes, ends at the release, or is cancelled. `state` is 'began', 'changed', 'ended' or 'cancelled'. `translation` is the movement since the drag began, in pixels: the travel the drag needed to begin is not part of it, so an element that follows it does not jump. `velocity` is in pixels per second; at 'ended' it is the release velocity (0 when the finger rested before lifting), and at 'cancelled' it is 0. Read through a ref: a new function each render re-creates nothing.
params.name: options.onPan

returns.description: Nothing: the hook hands out no recognizer. Without React, `createPanGesture(element, options)` takes the same options and returns `{destroy}`, which removes every listener it added and cancels a drag in progress.
returns.name: void

accessibility.description: A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons, arrow keys or a menu.
accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology

accessibility.description: The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: a settle or a throw goes to its end without travel when the person asks for reduced motion.
accessibility.name: Reduce Motion

bestPractices.description: Move the element from `translation` added to where it was when the drag began, so it moves with the finger from the moment the drag claims it.
At `ended`, hand `velocity` to the animation that settles the element, so a flick carries on at the speed it was released.
Give every drag another way to do the same thing from a keyboard and from assistive technology, such as buttons, arrow keys or a menu.
Use a component's own prop when it covers the job: BottomSheet's `snapPoints` for a sheet, Carousel's `hasSnap` for paging.
Hold the drag offset in a large component’s state: each `changed` event renders the component that holds it.
Recognize taps or long presses with it; `useLongPress` and the components’ own press handling own those.

usage.description: Reports a drag on an element as values, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap, and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. With `axis`, a scroll across that axis that starts on the element stays the page’s; without it, the pan takes a drag in any direction, so a finger’s scroll that starts on the element moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page. The hook is a thin layer over `createPanGesture`, the same API for code without React. A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons or arrow keys (WCAG 2.5.7). The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: honor the user’s reduced-motion setting in the animation that moves the element. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet’s `snapPoints`, Carousel’s `hasSnap`.

dense.description: Headless click-triggered popovers w/ focus trap, auto-focus, light dismiss, Escape, optional hidden close button. Every surface emits the canonical popover target. Custom compositions needing a distinct seam pass/document an owned surfaceTarget.

paramDescriptions.anchorRef: ref to the element popover sits on when not the trigger; read on open, each render and each show(); position only, no trigger ARIA or handlers.
paramDescriptions.dialogLabel: accessible label for popover dialog (role="dialog" only).
paramDescriptions.hasAutoFocus: focus genuine content on open; dialog surface fallback; generated close excluded.
paramDescriptions.hasCloseButton: whether hidden keyboard close button is included.
paramDescriptions.hasEscapeDismiss: whether Escape dismisses; full effect only w/ hasLightDismiss false or tabBehavior 'pageOrder'.
paramDescriptions.isModal: whether a dialog-role popover is modal (aria-modal); Tab stays inside either way.
paramDescriptions.onHide: fires when popover hides; focus a specific element here to send focus there (focus return then leaves it).
paramDescriptions.padding: spacing-scale padding on the painted surface; omit for none.
paramDescriptions.role: content wrapper ARIA role; "none" for listbox/menu popups.
paramDescriptions.surfaceTarget: optional owned refinement target; document it when distinct reachability is needed.
paramDescriptions.tabBehavior: 'contain' cycles Tab inside; 'pageOrder' lets Tab pass through in page order (popover after its trigger, or after a focusable anchor when it has no trigger; needs browser popover invokers; lost until it reopens when another layer opened from the same element closes), scopes Escape to focus in the popover or on its trigger/anchor, never aria-modal.
paramDescriptions.xstyle: StyleX styles for content wrapper, after default surface.

returnDescriptions.contentRef: content container ref for focus trap.
returnDescriptions.show: show popover; skipAutoFocus preserves current focus.
returnDescriptions.triggerRef: trigger ref for CSS anchor positioning.

bestPractices.description: Use for menus, pickers, forms, command panels needing focus management.
Prefer Popover for standard trigger-content pairs; use hook for custom trigger patterns.
Use the canonical popover target for broad surface theming.
For component-specific reachability, pass and document an owned surfaceTarget; it refines the same surface.
Use for non-interactive hover previews: use useHoverCard / useTooltip instead.

usage.description: Headless click-triggered popovers w/ focus trap, auto-focus, light dismiss, Escape, optional hidden close button. Every surface emits the canonical popover target. Custom compositions needing a distinct seam pass/document an owned surfaceTarget.

params.description: External ref to use as the popover anchor: the element the popover sits on when it is not the trigger. Any element with a CSS box works (an HTML element or an <svg> element; a shape inside an <svg> warns in development). The trigger keeps its toggle and ARIA; the anchor gets neither and is never a trigger. The ref is read on open, on each render of your component, and on each show(). To move an open popover, set anchorRef.current and call show(). A show() while the ref holds no element waits, and opens when the ref is next read and holds one. With no trigger attached, open it with show(). Omit it and the trigger is the anchor.
params.name: anchorRef

params.description: Callback fired when the popover becomes visible.
params.name: onShow

params.description: Callback fired when the popover is hidden. Focus returns on its own as the popover closes, and there is no option to turn that off; to send focus somewhere else, focus that element here.
params.name: onHide

params.description: StyleX styles applied to the popover content wrapper, after the default surface styles.
params.name: xstyle

dense.description: Marks an element as a pressable surface of the touch press model, tracked like a UIKit control (highlight as the finger lands, 150 ms inside a scroller, fade at the lift), and installs the shared document controller; on a coarse primary pointer it also paints mouse, trackpad and Space-key presses at once. Returns the data-astryx-pressable marker to spread; compose one of interactionOverlayStyles on the same element to paint.

returnDescriptions.pressableProps: marker attribute to spread on the painting element; compose one of interactionOverlayStyles (backgroundColor, backgroundImage, pressedBackgroundColor) there, which paints the press on every pointer; themed through --color-overlay-pressed.

Track the press with your own pointer listeners or state, or call it on an Astryx component (already marked).

usage.description: For a local component that paints its own press and must match Astryx under a finger. No per-element listener or state; one controller per document.

returns.description: The marker attribute to spread on the element that paints the press. Compose one of `interactionOverlayStyles` (from `@astryxdesign/core/utils`) on the same element — `backgroundColor` or `backgroundImage` for a surface whose hover and press are the system's overlays, `pressedBackgroundColor` for one whose hover is its own — and it paints the pressed token on the first frame of a press and fades it over the release, keeping `:active` for a mouse on a desktop. On a phone or tablet, where the stylesheet drops `:active`, the controller also paints a mouse, trackpad or Space-key press: at once, held while the button or key is down, faded at the release. A press is themed through `--color-overlay-pressed`.
returns.name: pressableProps

bestPractices.description: Spread the result on the element whose background paints the press and compose one of `interactionOverlayStyles` on it; the composed style is the instant onset, the hold and the fade, and it is themed through `--color-overlay-pressed`.

Let the composed style own the press on every pointer: it keeps `:active` for a desktop mouse and drops it under `@media (pointer: coarse)`, where the controller paints every press (a finger through the press model, a mouse or Space key at once). A rule of your own that paints `:active` would paint under a finger too, on the touch and through a scroll.
Add a pointer listener or React state to the element to track the press; the controller already writes the attribute, and per-element listeners are what a long list cannot afford.
Call it for a control rendered by an Astryx component; those are marked already, and the innermost marked element takes the press.

usage.description: The touch press model every Astryx pressable uses, for a local component that paints its own press. Under a finger, CSS `:active` paints on the touch itself and can outlive the start of a scroll; the press model instead tracks the touch the way UIKit tracks a control: it highlights as the finger lands (after the content-touch delay inside a scroller, where a flick paints nothing), a quick tap answers at the lift, and a scroll that takes the touch cancels it with no fade. One document-level controller does this for every marked element (installed by the first pressable to mount, removed by the last to unmount), so calling the hook adds no listener or state to your element. On a desktop a mouse press is still your `:active` rule: keep it, and drop it under `@media (pointer: coarse)` the way the built-in components do. That query reads the primary pointer, so on a phone or tablet it also drops `:active` for a connected mouse, trackpad or keyboard; the controller paints those presses there (at once, faded at the release), so nothing goes unanswered.

usage.description: Locks page scroll while active and keeps the page where it is. The page gets overflow: hidden (on the root, or on body when its own overflow is the one the viewport uses), which stops wheel, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling, and overscroll-behavior-y: none on the root and body, which stops the overscroll bounce while the lock holds. Where the primary pointer is coarse (phones and tablets), a one-finger pan that would scroll the page is cancelled, because iOS Safari scrolls an overflow: hidden page under a finger; pans that a scroller inside the overlay can take, drags on a native range input, pinch-zoom, and one-finger drags on a pinch-zoomed page (which pan the zoomed view) still work. The scroll offset never changes, so nothing jumps when the lock starts or ends, and iOS Safari keeps its toolbar as it was. Where the hidden scrollbar takes layout space (desktop), the hook holds its gutter open with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page, including any position: fixed chrome, does not shift sideways.

dense.description: Geometry-only column windowing opt-in for Table.virtualization. Keep full data, columns and a stable idKey on Table. Declared widths set the window; pinned columns always mount; a wide enough scroll area mounts every column. Unsupported content or structure renders every column. Native mounted-cell semantics, not discovery of unmounted columns. Adding or removing the capability remounts the table.
