bestPractices.description: Start with immediate behavior. Add, remove, and bulk changes call onChange as they occur and moves call the reorderable object's onReorder, and closing or dismissing the popover keeps those committed changes.
Set commitBehavior="staged" when the complete selection should be reviewed or persisted as one transaction. Apply commits a changed draft; Cancel, Escape, and light dismiss discard it.

Use TransferList directly inside ComplexSelector only when the surface needs custom structure such as saved views, presets, headers, or footer actions. Keep applied and draft state separate and reset the draft whenever the surface opens.

Use isTransferDisabled and the reorderable object's isReorderable independently: isTransferDisabled pins an option to its panel, and isReorderable keeps an option in its place. Provide disabledMessage when a transfer is unavailable so the constraint is discoverable; a row that keeps its place shows no reorder handle, so say why in its content when it matters.

With no `reorderable`, TransferList no longer reorders; pass `reorderable={createReorderable(…)}`. Migrating from isReorderable: pass reorderable={createReorderable({onReorder, isReorderable})} instead. The isReorderable prop and each option's isReorderDisabled are gone; return false from the object's isReorderable(value) for an option that stays put.
Keep rows concise and single-line. Use option description as searchable metadata, or renderOption when richer visible content is necessary.

Commit add, remove, and bulk changes immediately. A drag leaves the rows still: the row dims in place, a copy of it follows the finger or pointer, and an insertion line marks where it would land; the reorderable object's onReorder runs once on release.
Use commitBehavior as a presentation or container choice. Both values render the same selector popover; use explicit composition for a different shell.
Use a transfer list for a handful of simple choices; CheckboxInput or MultiSelector is more compact.

usage.description: Use TransferListSelector by default for medium-to-large, inspectable sets where membership and selected order need explicit control. Immediate behavior commits each edit and renders no footer. Choose staged behavior when users must review a set of changes before Apply. Use TransferList directly only in a deliberately custom ComplexSelector surface, such as table column settings with saved views and a custom footer.

props.name: markdownExtensions

props.description: CodeBlock language values a fence may name, each imported on its own (e.g. graphql from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/graphql) or made with createCodeLanguage. Pass the same list as Markdown codeLanguages so a matched fence paints and labels the same while reading and editing. RichTextView takes the same prop.
props.name: codeLanguages

props.description: Markdown transformers: the single source of truth for markdown behaviour. Defaults to thematic breaks, the standard @lexical/markdown TRANSFORMERS (with each nested list written at the content column of the item above it, so it reads back nested), hard line breaks (a line break typed with Shift+Enter exports as a backslash before the line ending, so it reads back as a line break), and GFM tables; a custom array replaces the default, thematic breaks and tables included. In Lexical the same array drives all three markdown operations (shortcut typing, markdown->state import, state->markdown export); this prop wires shortcut typing today and is the intended input for the serialization APIs added in later phases. Pass a custom array to support additional node types (e.g. transformers layered in via the nodes extension point) consistently across all three. Shortcut typing is only applied when hasMarkdownShortcuts is true.
props.name: transformers

props.description: Automatically focus the editor on mount.
props.name: hasAutoFocus

props.default: 'Press Escape then Tab to move focus out of the editor.' (translated)
props.description: Screen-reader hint describing how to move focus out of the editor, since Tab is bound to indentation (press Escape, then Tab). Visually hidden, wired via aria-describedby. Translated for the active locale; override to change the text, or pass "" to omit.
props.name: tabEscapeHint

props.description: Maximum number of characters. When set, a character counter (current/max) is displayed below the editor. Like TextArea, does not enforce the limit natively; the counter shows error styling when the plain-text length exceeds the limit.
props.name: maxLength

props.description: Width of the field. Numbers are pixels, strings used as-is (e.g. "100%").
props.name: width

props.description: Minimum height of the editable content surface. Numbers are pixels; strings are used as CSS lengths. Content continues growing beyond this height.
props.name: minHeight

props.description: The Lexical composer namespace, used for editor identity.
props.name: namespace

props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.
props.name: xstyle

bestPractices.description: RichText is built on Lexical and exposes it: nodes and transformers take Lexical types, plugins takes Lexical React plugins, and onChange and getEditorState() report Lexical types. Install the lexical and @lexical/* peers (optional peers) at the Lexical minor named in the package peer ranges before importing from @astryxdesign/richtext.
Persist content by serializing editorState.toJSON() in onChange; rehydrate via defaultValue / RichTextView value.
Register custom node types via the nodes prop on BOTH the editor and the RichTextView so serialized content round-trips.

Use a ref (RichTextEditorRef) to imperatively focus(), clear(), read the state via getEditorState(), serialize to Markdown via getMarkdown() or HTML via getHTML(), or reach the LexicalEditor via getEditor(). The handle is available after mount. getMarkdown() uses the same transformers prop the editor is configured with, and returns imported content as it was written: blocks nobody changed come back byte for byte, and only blocks that were edited or added are written in canonical Markdown. focus() and clear() are no-ops when the editor is read-only or disabled, and clear() resets to a single empty paragraph.

GFM pipe tables import, edit, and export by default. The first row renders as header cells, delimiter-row colons set each column alignment, rows shorter than the widest row gain empty cells, and a wide table scrolls inside its own wrapper. Arrow keys move between cells; Tab keeps its editor meaning, so Escape then Tab still leaves the editor. Pasting a table into a table fills its cells one by one from the cell holding the caret, or within the selected cells, adding rows and columns as needed; a cell the paste does not fill keeps its text, and a table pasted with other content goes into the cell as text. Tables export in the canonical form: outer pipes and three-dash delimiters. RichTextView renders the same tables. Install @lexical/table with the other lexical peers.

In a code block, Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent every line the selection touches, by the indent the block already uses: a tab when one of its lines starts with a tab, otherwise the fewest spaces an indented line starts with (2 to 8), otherwise 2 spaces. The selection stays on the same characters, and each press is one undo step. Escape then Tab still moves focus out of the editor.

Backspace at the very start of a code block turns it into a paragraph holding its lines, each on its own line, with the caret at its start. The code never merges into the block above, so a heading above keeps its own text. Backspace anywhere else in a code block deletes as usual.

Pasting into a code block inserts plain code. Rich content, such as a web page, a word processor document, or blocks copied from another editor, goes in as the plain text on the clipboard; when the clipboard has no plain text, each pasted block goes in as one line of its text. Headings, lists, tables, and formatting never land inside a code block.

Cmd+A (Ctrl+A on other platforms) in a code block or a table cell selects the code or the cell text first; pressing it again selects the whole document. Anywhere else it selects the whole document at once.

Thematic breaks (---, ***, ___, with or without spaces between) import as horizontal rules and export as ---. A dash line directly under a paragraph line stays with that paragraph, as in Markdown. Click a rule or arrow onto it to select it; Backspace removes it. RichTextView draws the same rules. Install @lexical/extension with the other lexical peers.

To produce a defaultValue from Markdown without mounting an editor (e.g. on the server), use markdownToEditorStateJSON(markdown). Convert the other way with editorStateJSONToMarkdown(json). Both run headless via @lexical/headless and accept the same transformers/nodes options as the editor. The round trip keeps the Markdown as written: exporting unchanged content returns the input exactly, including indentation, escapes, character references, fence metadata, and constructs the editor shows as plain text, and an edit regenerates only the blocks it changed. On the server or in Node, import them from @astryxdesign/richtext/markdown, which loads no React or client code.

To recognize a Markdown plugin made with createMarkdownPlugin, adopt it with createRichTextExtension(plugin) and pass the result in the extensions option of markdownToEditorStateJSON. Core's parser finds the plugin's syntax, and each node keeps its exact source, which is what it exports; base Markdown inside plugin source stays part of the node. A plugin that declares a transform is refused with a RichTextExtensionError, and so is a configuration that adopts one plugin twice. Without the extension, plugin syntax stays text. createRichTextExtension and the serializers are also exported from @astryxdesign/richtext/markdown for server code. Pass the same extensions to the markdownExtensions prop of RichTextEditor and RichTextView to draw the nodes: each renders as core Markdown renders it, edits as one unit (the caret steps over it; Backspace, cut, copy, and paste take it whole), and exports its exact source.

Add a formatting toolbar with toolbar={<RichTextEditorToolbar />}. The dedicated slot places it edge-to-edge at the top of the field, before the padded editing surface, with a RichText-owned 4px control gutter and correct keyboard order. It uses small Astryx Toolbar controls: undo/redo, a divided block-format Selector for paragraphs/headings/lists/quotes, then divided inline ToggleButtons for bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/code and links. The complete action row scrolls horizontally when space is tight, keeping every control directly available without a More menu. The Selector keeps its default adaptive placement. Compose extra controls via endContent.

Links: the toolbar Link button (on by default; disable with hasLink={false}) and Cmd/Ctrl+K open a non-modal Astryx Popover anchored to the button. It holds one URL field, applied with Enter, and Apply, Remove (when the selection is in a link), and Cancel icon buttons with tooltips. It keeps the Lexical selection while focus is in the field: Escape or Cancel closes it and returns focus and the selection to the editor, and a URL that cannot be linked shows an error under the field, which keeps focus. Pass promptForUrl only when integrating an existing synchronous URL flow; it replaces the popover. Entered URLs are sanitized (only http/https/mailto/tel are written; javascript:/data: are rejected). Links open in a new tab by default: target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer are written into the link node data; set hasNewTabLinks={false} for same-tab links. The toolbar takes base props and passes them to the Astryx Toolbar it renders: ref, className, style and xstyle on its root; data-*, other aria-* attributes and DOM handlers on the toolbar element (name it with label, not aria-label).

Auto-linking: render RichTextEditorAutoLinkPlugin in the plugins slot to turn typed/pasted URLs and emails into links automatically. Created links open in a new tab by default (target=_blank, rel=noopener noreferrer, baked into the node). Pass matchers to recognize additional patterns (build them with createLinkMatcherWithRegExp).

The toolbar's glyphs are themeable. Each control resolves its icon from the theme icons, else the `registerIcons()` registry, under a stable richtext:* key (see RICHTEXT_ICON_KEYS), falling back to a bundled inline SVG. A theme restyles any glyph without forking the toolbar by naming its key: defineTheme({icons: {'richtext:bold': <MyBoldIcon />}}). Undo and redo mirror under right-to-left direction, whichever glyph draws them.

To switch between reading (Markdown or RichTextView) and editing the same document in place, give the editor's field its inset and border outside the reading width, so every paragraph keeps its line count across the switch. Define the frame with stylex.create, for example const inPlace = stylex.create({editorFrame: {marginInline: `calc(-1 * (${spacingVars['--spacing-2']} + ${borderVars['--border-width']}))`}}), with spacingVars and borderVars from @astryxdesign/core/theme/tokens.stylex, and pass xstyle={inPlace.editorFrame} to the RichTextEditor. The recipe assumes no status: a status icon reserves another spacing-6 at the inline end. The field then extends past the column on both sides; leave room for it in the surrounding padding. A standalone editor in a form keeps its default width, so its border lines up with the fields around it.
Use for single-line input or plain text; use TextInput or TextArea for those.

usage.description: A WYSIWYG rich-text editor built on Lexical, styled with Astryx design tokens. Its field container shares TextArea input visuals for the resting border, hover ring, focus-within ring, disabled state, and status colors. Ships from @astryxdesign/richtext; lexical and @lexical/* are optional peer dependencies. The editor is deliberately minimal and extensible: pass toolbar, nodes, and plugins to layer richer behaviour (formatting, mentions, hover cards) on top without forking. Use RichTextView to render serialized content read-only.

doc.description: Turns typed and pasted URLs and email addresses into links, in the plugins slot of RichTextEditor.
doc.name: RichTextEditorAutoLinkPlugin

props.description: Link matchers to use. The default recognizes URLs and email addresses and opens the links in a new tab. Build extra matchers with createLinkMatcherWithRegExp from @lexical/react/LexicalAutoLinkPlugin.
props.name: matchers

props.description: Called when auto-linking creates, updates or removes a link. It gets the new URL, or null when the link is removed, and the previous URL.
props.name: onChange
props.type: (url: string | null, prevUrl: string | null) => void

bestPractices.description: Pass it as plugins={<RichTextEditorAutoLinkPlugin />}. Its links open in a new tab, with target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" in the node.
Render it outside RichTextEditor's plugins slot: it needs the editor's Lexical composer.

usage.description: Turns typed and pasted URLs and email addresses into links. Text inside a code block stays code and is never linked. Render it in RichTextEditor's plugins slot; it reaches the editor through the editor's Lexical composer and uses AutoLinkNode, which the editor registers by default.

doc.description: Formatting toolbar for the toolbar slot of RichTextEditor.
doc.name: RichTextEditorToolbar

props.description: Ref to the toolbar's root element. The ref, className, style and xstyle reach the root of the Astryx Toolbar it renders; data-*, other aria-* attributes and DOM handlers reach its role="toolbar" element.
props.name: ref

props.description: Accessible label for the toolbar element. Pass label rather than aria-label.
props.name: label

props.description: Which heading levels the block-format selector offers, in order.
props.name: headingLevels

props.description: Size of the toolbar's controls; it also sets the toolbar's padding.
props.name: size

props.description: Whether to show the link button. It opens a link popover anchored to the button, with one URL field applied with Enter and Remove when the selection is in a link. The popover is not modal; Escape or Cancel returns focus and the selection to the editor. With a collapsed selection the URL is inserted as link text; otherwise the selected text is linked. Only http, https, mailto and tel URLs are written.
props.name: hasLink

props.description: A synchronous URL prompt that replaces the built-in link popover when the link button is pressed on a selection that is not a link. It gets the selected text; return the URL, or null or an empty string to cancel.
props.name: promptForUrl

props.description: Whether links made with the toolbar open in a new tab. When true, target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" are written into the link node, so they serialize.
props.name: hasNewTabLinks

props.description: Extra items at the end of the toolbar, after a divider, such as mention or AI controls.
props.name: endContent

props.description: StyleX styles for the toolbar's root.
props.name: xstyle

bestPractices.description: Pass it as toolbar={<RichTextEditorToolbar />}. The slot places it at the top of the field, before the editing surface, in the right keyboard order.
Restyle a glyph from a theme by its richtext:* icon key (see RICHTEXT_ICON_KEYS), for example defineTheme({icons: {'richtext:bold': <MyBoldIcon />}}).
Render it outside RichTextEditor's toolbar slot: it needs the editor's Lexical composer.

usage.description: A formatting toolbar for RichTextEditor, built from Astryx Toolbar, Selector and ToggleButton controls: undo and redo, a block-format selector for paragraphs, headings, lists and quotes, inline bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and code, and links. Render it in the editor's toolbar slot; it reaches the editor through the editor's Lexical composer, so it must live inside it.

props.description: Serialized editor state to render: the JSON string from JSON.stringify(editorState.toJSON()). The view updates when value changes.
props.name: value

props.description: Lexical nodes to register beyond the default set. Pass the same nodes the content was authored with, so custom node types deserialize.
props.name: nodes

props.description: Markdown plugins whose nodes this view draws, each adopted with createRichTextExtension. A plugin node renders as core Markdown renders it; a node whose plugin is not passed shows its source. Pass the extensions the content was converted with, created in a client module.
props.name: markdownExtensions

props.description: CodeBlock languages a fence may name, such as graphql from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/graphql. Pass the same list as Markdown's codeLanguages, so reading and editing label and paint the same languages.
props.name: codeLanguages

props.description: Read-only Lexical plugins to render inside the view, such as hover cards or decorators.
props.name: plugins

props.description: The Lexical composer namespace.
props.name: namespace

props.description: Called when value cannot be parsed or rendered, for example malformed JSON or a node type that is not registered through nodes. Use it to log or report the failure.
props.name: onParseError

props.description: What to render when value cannot be parsed or rendered. The view renders it instead of throwing.
props.name: errorFallback

props.description: StyleX styles for the view root.
props.name: xstyle

bestPractices.description: Store editorState.toJSON() from RichTextEditor onChange, and pass the stringified JSON as value.
Register the same custom nodes and markdownExtensions on the editor and the view, so stored content round-trips.
Pass onParseError and an errorFallback when the stored content can come from an older or a foreign schema. By default a parse failure renders nothing instead of throwing.
Use RichTextView to render Markdown source; use core Markdown for that.

usage.description: Renders serialized RichTextEditor content read-only, with the same nodes, tables, code blocks and Markdown plugin nodes the editor draws. Ships from @astryxdesign/richtext, with lexical and @lexical/* as optional peer dependencies.
